articles.title: How Jadumani Singh's risky weight change nearly derailed his CWG dream before winning Glasgow silver
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: When Indian pugilist Jadumani Singh Mandengbam stepped onto the podium to receive the men's 55kg silver medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Game.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When Indian pugilist Jadumani Singh Mandengbam stepped onto the podium to receive the men's 55kg silver medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, it marked the culmination of a journey that had almost ended before it had even begun.The 22-year-old Manipuri boxer was one of India's standout performers, winning four consecutive unanimous 5-0 verdicts to storm into the bantamweight final before settling for silver against Australia's Jye Dixon. His medal also formed part of India's historic boxing campaign, which yielded seven golds and three silvers, making the country the No. 1 boxing nation at the Games for the first time.Yet, behind that success lay months of uncertainty, selection hurdles and a weight-category gamble that nearly cost him a place on the flight to Scotland.Speaking exclusively to TimesofIndia.com, former world champion and Jadumani's mentor, Laishram Sarita Devi, recounted how the young boxer refused to abandon his Olympic dream even when every obstacle seemed stacked against him.A bold gamble after the 50kg category disappearedJadumani had built his reputation in the 50kg category, winning medals at World Boxing Cups before learning that the division would no longer feature in the Commonwealth Games, Asian Games or Olympic programme.Rather than remain in a non-Olympic category, he decided to move up to 55kg â a division already occupied by some of India's biggest names."He continued to consult with me. Whenever he had to make a big decision, he called up and consulted with me â like increasing his weight category," Sarita told TimesofIndia.com."After he won a World Cup medal in 50kg, he got to know that the weight category is no longer in the CWG, Asian Games and Olympics. He wanted to move to 55kg."The decision immediately brought fresh challenges."Army had their No. 1 boxer in the 55kg category in Pune, who is Services' No. 1 boxer. And the weight category also has Amit Panghal â Olympian and Asian champion. He said he wanted to move up the weight to compete at CWG, Asian Games etc, but was discouraged by hearing questions like whether he would be able to compete at that level, which created a doubt in him," she said.Sarita, however, wanted only one answer: "We sat down and I asked him, 'Are you confident about the decision?' He said he was, so I told him to move up the category."The selection maze before GlasgowThe decision created another problem.Without competing in the National Championships, Jadumani could not enter the national coaching camp. But because he belonged to the Army Sports Institute, Services already had its designated 55kg representative. Attempts to let him represent Manipur also failed."We tried to make him compete for the state of Manipur, but we didn't get an NOC because he is with the Army," Sarita said.Relief finally arrived through a Boxing Federation of India (BFI) policy that granted direct entries to the National Championships for World Boxing Cup medallists. The move was aimed at rewarding elite international performers and ensuring they were not blocked by the usual domestic qualification pathways.The decision allowed Jadumani to compete directly in the 55kg draw despite the institutional overlap, resulting in multiple squad members â Pawan Bartwal, Jadumani Singh and Amit Panghal â finding themselves in the same weight-category draw.Sarita said her ward grabbed the opportunity with both hands."He then got a chance to compete in 55kg in the Nationals. Due to his effort, he won against the Services No.1, Olympians etc to be named Best Boxer in the Nationals. After that he got the chance to be part of the India camp," she said.He then cleared the final selection trials, which included physical assessments alongside ring performances."He participated in the final trial for the CWG and Asian Games â which had many aspects like strength and endurance tests before fighting in the ring. He won all of it to get selected for the CWG and was really happy and started training hard," she added.The Sports Ministry hurdleJust when Glasgow appeared certain, another setback emerged.Because Jadumani had only recently moved into 55kg, he did not possess the Asian ranking required under the Sports Ministry's eligibility criteria for Commonwealth Games selection."He got an explanation mail from the Sports Ministry, which put him in immense tension ahead of the Games," Sarita recalled.Under the ministry's guidelines, boxers were expected to be ranked among Asia's top eight in their respective categories."He was ranked No. 2 in 50kg, but he lacked a ranking in the new 55kg category. He had only competed in one Asian Championship in the new weight category before the trials for CWG and, being new to the category, lost in the quarterfinals," she said.That led to fresh doubts over his selection."He was disheartened when questions were raised whether he was a medal prospect because he was not in the rankings prescribed by the ministry. He called me and said the coaches were saying he may or may not be on the flight to the CWG because of this letter from the ministry," she recalled.The uncertainty only ended after BFI submitted a detailed explanation to the ministry, outlining Jadumani's circumstances following his weight-category switch."BFI replied to the ministry properly, explaining everything and after a lot of effort his ticket to Glasgow was approved. What I like about him is that he is the kind of person who doesn't give up and has a very strong will power," she said.Why the gold slipped awayJadumani eventually reached the final after four demanding contests, each won by an identical 5-0 margin. But Sarita believes the scheduling ultimately worked against him."Jadumani's four bouts were very tough. He played all out in all the bouts till the semifinals as he got proper rest and recovery time. Since the gold medal opponent got a bye earlier, he had fewer bouts than Jadumani," she explained.The semifinal-final turnaround, she felt, proved decisive. There was a one-day gap after every bout until the semifinals, but there was no gap between the semifinal and final in Glasgow."Jadumani fought his semifinal in the evening and got the final bout the next morning only, so he did not get much time for recovery. If it was in the evening, he could have fought better. When he entered the ring for the final, I saw his face and body language sitting here and realised he had not had enough recovery," she said.The experience, she believes, underlines the growing importance of sports science."In such situations, we should look for how we can enhance or speed up the recovery process through sports science. We should discuss it to make sure our boxers can give 100 per cent every time they enter the ring," she added.Olympic gold remains the ultimate dreamSarita first noticed Jadumani as a youngster competing in a local tournament."When I saw Jadumani for the first time, it was a tournament for young boys. His movement was really pleasing and I thought he could become a good boxer in the future. I identified him at that time only and gave him Rs 500 because I was very pleased with his performance," she recalled."Jadumani did not start with me from the grassroots. He learnt his basics from another academy. He came to my academy when he was preparing to enrol in the Army Sports Institute in Pune. At that time, I did not have any infrastructure and was coaching from a makeshift setup. And then Covid happened, we had to train in a very isolated small makeshift place,â she added.Years later, after training together through difficult Covid-19 conditions and watching him overcome one hurdle after another, Sarita believes Glasgow is only the beginning."We missed gold at the CWG, but we will work hard to get gold at the Asian Games for sure," she said.The bigger ambition, however, stretches far beyond continental success."His first and primary target remains Olympic gold. Commonwealth Games and Asian Games are the stepping stones in that journey. He will try to win India's first Olympic gold medal in boxing," Sarita concluded.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From hospital bed to CWG gold: How Jaismine Lamboria fought the odds in Glasgow
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Just weeks before stepping into the ring at the Commonwealth Games, Jaismine Lamboria wasnât thinking about medals. She was searching for a.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Just weeks before stepping into the ring at the Commonwealth Games, Jaismine Lamboria wasnât thinking about medals. She was searching for answers. The recurring fever had refused to go away.Multiple medical tests showed nothing unusual and the Indian boxer tried to push through, managing the symptoms with paracetamol. When the illness persisted, she was admitted to a hospital in Mohali. Doctors finally diagnosed a bacterial infection, putting her on an intensive 14-day course of medication. For an athlete preparing for one of the biggest competitions of the year, it could easily have been the end of the campaign.Instead, it became the beginning of one of the most remarkable comebacks of her career. âI was avoiding further medical tests because the initial reports were coming back normal. We didnât know what exactly had to be treated. Finally, after I was admitted, they detected a bacterial infection and I was on medication for 14 days,â the 57kg boxer said.When she was discharged, the clock was already ticking. Barely three weeks remained before the Games. âI started training only on July 1. Initially it was just warm-up, walking and stretching. I had very little time, so we had to be patient.âThe physical recovery was only one part of the challenge. During those uncertain weeks, sports psychologist Priya Vrinda became a constant source of support, ensuring the illness didnât break her confidence.âWhen I was sick, I was already connected with Priya Vrinda maâam. She kept me mentally strong and never allowed me to go down,â Jaismine said. That resilience was evident when she returned to competition. Jaismine boxed with maturity, tactical discipline and composure to upgrade the Commonwealth bronze she had won four years ago into gold in the 57kg.One of Jaismineâs biggest assets inside the ring has been her reach in her category. While every opponent may not be shorter â Jaismine stands five feet seven inches in her socks â she believes her physical advantage has become an important weapon thanks to careful coaching. âMy coaches taught me how to use my reach properly. It definitely gives me an advantage in many bouts.âGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Watch: PM Modi meets CWG medallists, says âJo khelega, woh khilegaâ
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Indiaâs Commonwealth Games 2026 medal winners at his residence in New Delhi on Sunday and congratulated them for thei.
articles.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Indiaâs Commonwealth Games 2026 medal winners at his residence in New Delhi on Sunday and congratulated them for their performances in Glasgow. The meeting came shortly after India finished fourth in the Gamesâ overall medal standings.Soon after the interaction, Modi shared a video from the meeting on X with the caption, "Always #Cheer4Bharat." The video showed gold medallist boxer Sakshi Chaudhary and other members of Indiaâs medal-winning contingent.In the video, Sakshi said, "Hello friends! This is Sakshi Chaudhary. Today, our honourable Prime Minister has invited us, the Commonwealth Games medalists, and we feel very proud. We are extremely happy to have met him; he is very humble. Sir, would you like to say something?"Modi responded, "Jo khelega, woh khilega" (The one who plays, will blossom). Always cheer for Bharat." He later led the athletes in chanting "Bharat Mata ki Jai" three times.Indiaâs Glasgow campaignIndia finished the Commonwealth Games with 39 medals â 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze â despite sending a much smaller contingent than in Birmingham 2022. India had 122 athletes in Glasgow compared with 210 in Birmingham, while 30 of Birminghamâs 61 medals came in sports that were not included this time.Despite fewer opportunities, India retained fourth place and had 38 athletes return with medals. Gulveer Singh was the only Indian athlete to win two medals.The Glasgow Games also marked the handover of the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India, which will host the centenary edition in Ahmedabad in 2030.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: âThat video was not ordinaryâ: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.âKya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)â Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.âWe had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,â she explained.âThat video was not ordinaryâModi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.âTo be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,â he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics.Mirabai opens up about four difficult yearsModi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.âItne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),â Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.âI was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.âThere were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,â she said.Narender's joke leaves Modi laughingThe meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.âDuring the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),â he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.âI have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.âFar more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,â Modi said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: A Pakistani boxer's unusual reaction after losing to Indian heavyweight Narender Berwal left Prime Minister Narendra Modi amused during an .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Pakistani boxer's unusual reaction after losing to Indian heavyweight Narender Berwal left Prime Minister Narendra Modi amused during an interaction with India's Commonwealth Games 2026 medallists on Sunday.Berwal, who won silver in the men's 90+kg category in Glasgow, recalled an incident from his boxing career when he defeated a Pakistani opponent at the 2015 World Military Games. The boxer said his opponent was left bewildered by the repeated appearance of the name 'Narender' in his life.âMujhe Narendra naam se nafrat ho gayi haiâRecalling the exchange with Modi, Berwal said: âPakistani boxer said to me, 'Aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narendra hai. Mujhe Narendra naam se nafrat ho gayi hai'...âThe anecdote was part of a light-hearted interaction between Modi and India's medal winners at his residence in New Delhi. The Prime Minister congratulated the athletes for their performances and heard them recount some of the most memorable moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Berwal's silver was part of India's historic boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games. The Indian boxers returned from Glasgow with 10 medals, including seven golds and three silvers â their best-ever haul at the Games.India finished fourth overall in Glasgow with 39 medals â 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze â despite competing in a smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme.Jadumani's Kargil connectionAnother boxer, Jadumani Singh, shared a more emotional story from Glasgow, recalling his victory over a Pakistani opponent on Kargil Vijay Diwas.Jadumani, who won silver in the men's 55kg category, defeated Pakistan's Sumama Rehman 5-0 in the round of 16. Speaking to Modi, the boxer, who is associated with the Indian Army, explained why the date made the victory particularly significant.âIt was Kargil Day. The day I fought against Pakistan was on that day. Being from the Indian Army, I was very determined that I had to beat Pakistan. I defeated them 5-0 and dedicated it to our Indian Army heroes,â Jadumani said.Modi praised the significance of the victory and its dedication to the Kargil heroes.âRemembering that, especially since you are from the forces yourself... I truly believe the sentiment you expressed, dedicating your medal to the Kargil winners, added extra glory to that victory. And you defeated exactly the one you were supposed to!â Modi said.The Glasgow Games concluded after 11 days of competition, with Scotland handing over the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India, which will host the 2030 edition in Ahmedabad.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rajasthan stuck in 2012, Manipur in 2023: How actively are states with CWG medals promoting sports?
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as s.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.Haryana: Hit on the podium, not so much off itNo state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Haryana Sports social media activityFacebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur still talking about 2023Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.Manipur Sports social media activityAnd yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. Itâs the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.Rajasthan: 14 years and countingIf there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Rajasthan Sports social media activityIts X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Uttar Pradesh and Delhi carry the same gloomy pictureGulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.UP Sports social media activityDelhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.And then come Tamil Nadu and othersSet against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.The ones somewhere in the middleNot every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.Does it matter so much?It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensationSilence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. paragraphs: NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.Haryana: Hit on the podium, not so much off itNo state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Haryana Sports social media activityFacebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur still talking about 2023Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.Manipur Sports social media activityAnd yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. Itâs the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.Rajasthan: 14 years and countingIf there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Rajasthan Sports social media activityIts X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Uttar Pradesh and Delhi carry the same gloomy pictureGulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.UP Sports social media activityDelhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.And then come Tamil Nadu and othersSet against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.The ones somewhere in the middleNot every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.Does it matter so much?It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensationSilence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Jonny Clayton claims second World Series of Darts title with commanding victory over compatriot Gerwyn Price in New Zealand Darts Masters final in Auckland; watch the World Grand Prix live from September 28 on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Jonny Clayton beat compatriot Gerwyn Price 8-4 to win the New Zealand Darts Masters in Auckland.

The Welshman defeated Gian van Veen and James Wade on his route to the final where he sealed his second World Series of Darts title with a 124-checkout finish on the bullseye.

Clayton hit a 158-finish to assume a 3-0 lead and never relinquished the advantage, racing into a 7-1 lead before holding off a late, three-leg rally to avenge his defeat to Price in the 2022 final in Hamilton.

  • Stream darts and more with NOW
  • When is darts live on Sky Sports?
  • Listen to the Love the Darts podcast

"It was great to play in the final with my World Cup partner," Clayton reflected.

"It just shows that two rugby boys can play darts, and to play against each other in the world of rugby here in New Zealand, I've got a smile on my face.

"I really enjoyed that. It's 1-1 now, so next year - winner takes all!

"I'm looking forward to Wollongong next week. Hopefully the sun will shine on me and I can lift another trophy!"

articles.title: European Athletics medal ceremonies postponed after police arrest, Great Britain relay team among those left at stadium
articles.summary: In a statement, Birmingham 2026 said: "Championship transport was suspended until the necessary security measures had been carried out whilst West Midlands Police arrested a man in his thirties on suspicion of fraud"
articles.body:
Amy Hunt and Dina Asher-Smith were among the athletes left stuck at the Alexander Stadium on Saturday night after a "police incident" suspended transport operations at the European Championships in Birmingham.

Organisers later confirmed in a statement that event transport was paused in order to carry out security measures, while West Midlands Police arrested a man in his 30s on suspicion of fraud.

The Press Association understands the athletes still left on site - including the British men's and women's 4×100m relay teams who had won gold in the final two events of the penultimate evening session - were sent back to the high performance centre next to the venue.

  • Glave: From 2022 in a back brace to European champion - 'Delayed but not denied'
  • European Athletics Championships 2026: Updates from Birmingham
  • England finish second in Commonwealth Games medal table
  • 'Ramsay-Peaty emotion showed what Commonwealth Games means'

When transport services did resume about one hour and 45 minutes later, those competing on Sunday were prioritised.

They include Hunt, who is hoping to complete an historic quadruple of European titles in a single championships with gold in the inaugural mixed 4x100m relay.

There was a heavy police presence outside the 23,000-capacity stadium, which had been near capacity, and huge static queues of spectators waiting for shuttle buses, some of whom took to social media to complain about a lack of information.

It is also understood the decision to cancel six medal ceremonies, due to take place between 10pm and 11pm, was related to the police incident.

A Birmingham 2026 statement, issued in the early hours of Sunday morning, read: "Birmingham 2026 can confirm that transport operations have returned to normal following a police incident on Saturday evening.

"Championship transport was suspended until the necessary security measures had been carried out while West Midlands Police arrested a man in his thirties on suspicion of fraud.

"The safety and wellbeing of our spectators, athletes, workforce and the wider Championships family will always be our first priority.

"We recognise that the delays presented challenges for those affected and would like to thank everyone for their patience, understanding and cooperation throughout the evening.

"Further information will be issued on Sunday relating to the evening's postponed medal ceremonies."

Members of the public who were not waiting for the shuttle buses were free to leave of their own accord, but the security concern was understood to be significant enough that West Midlands Police took over the situation.

A statement on the event's official account, posted on X at 11.03pm, apologised for the "significant delays" but did not explain the cause.

Media and other staff who were working in the stadium and the adjacent media facilities after the general public had left were allowed to remain in those areas.

No explanation was offered for what was happening outside the exits, but there was no indication anyone remaining at the venue was in any danger.

articles.title: WWE WrestleMania 42 Attendance Revealed, How Big Was Drop from WM 41 That Set All-Time Gate Record?
articles.summary: Official numbers from the Las Vegas Stadium Authority show WrestleMania 42 attendance was down roughly 15 percent from the previous year.
articles.body:
Official numbers from the Las Vegas Stadium Authority show WrestleMania 42 attendance was down roughly 15 percent from the previous year.

The Las Vegas Stadium Authority announced the two-day attendance for this year's WrestleMania was 97,126 with the split being 47,093 on Saturday and 50,033 on Sunday.

WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before Heatwave 2026

The attendance marks a drop of 21,515 from 2025, which was also the most financially successful pro wrestling show ever with a $66 million gate across the two nights.

WrestleMania 42 marks the first time since 2021, when attendance was still limited due to the COVID-19 pandemic, that WWE's marquee event did draw more than 100,000 fans for the two-night event.

Despite the drop in attendance, WWE and TKO have touted WrestleMania 42 as "one of the highest-grossing events in company history," including record or near-record figures across across gate, sponsorship, merchandise, WWE World, On Location VIP experiences and digital.

Last year's show was largely built around John Cena's heel turn and his chase to win a record-setting 17th world championship against Cody Rhodes. It was also Cena's first WrestleMania match since losing to Austin Theory in 2023.

WrestleMania 42 featured Rhodes defeating Randy Orton to retain the undisputed WWE title in the main event of night one and Roman Reigns beating CM Punk in the main event of night two to win the world heavyweight championship.

Next year's WrestleMania will be held in Saudi Arabia, marking the first time it has taken place outside of North America.

articles.title: AEW Dynamite Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights From Aug. 19
articles.summary: From the Chesapeake Employers Insurance Arena in Baltimore, Maryland on August 19, All Elite Wrestling presented the final Dynamite before heading overseas.
articles.body:
From the Chesapeake Employers Insurance Arena in Baltimore, Maryland on August 19, All Elite Wrestling presented the final Dynamite before heading overseas.

Will Ospreay and Kenny Omega battled The Don Callis Family in separate trios matches. Maya World defended the TBS Championship against Hikaru Shida, Kris Statlander and Persephone.

The Continental Challenge Cup continued with Jon Moxley vs. "Switchblade" Jay White and Nigel McGuinness vs. Hechicero.

Elsewhere on the show, Renee Paquette sat down with Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay, as well as Willow Nightingale and Mercedes Moné, ahead of their respective singles world title matches at All In.

Check out all the results including winners, grades and highlights for Dynamite below.

Will Ospreay, Francesco Akira and HENARE vs. Brian Cage, Lance Archer and Rocky Romero

Last Time in Action: Will Ospreay, Francesco Akira and HENARE alongside Callum Newman defeated The Death Riders (Dynamite, April 8). This was the first time Brian Cage, Lance Archer and Rocky Romero represented The Don Callis Family as a trio.

United Empire started with a strong pace set by the leadership of The Aerial Assassin including HENARE matching the power of Archer with his strikes.

The Murderhawk Monster fought back and laid out all three babyfaces into the commercial break.

The Don Callis Family kept control back from break until HENARE laid out Cage with a German Suplex and got the hot tag to Ospreay.

The Aerial Assassin teamed up with Akira for a Cutter on Rocky. HENARE and Akira then dived onto Archer and Cage outside while Ospreay hit Rocky with a Hidden Blade to win.

This was a fun opener, even if the result was blatantly obvious including the exact man that was always taking that Hidden Blade at the end.

The best part of the match was simply another opportunity for Akira and HENARE to show off, and they should appear more in AEW as their schedules allow.

The Aerial Assassin picked up some momentum and avoided taking any rough bumps along the way.

The real story for Ospreay just two Dynamites before All In was likely to play out later in the night.

Ospreay, Akira and HENARE def. Rocky, Archer and Cage by pinfall.

Excalibur ran down the card to start the show but seemed to get confused with what was starting, teasing The Elite before Ospreay arrived.

The excitement of Akira and HENARE is infectious. Both sold how much it meant to them to be working this match.

Callis and ICE got equal hate from the loud Baltimore crowd.

After the win, Opreay mouthed to the camera that Callum Newman needed to pick up his phone.

Konosuke Takeshita Returns to Lay Out Kyle Fletcher

Backstage, Kazuchika Okada spoke with Renee Paquette and explained that Kyle Fletcher should be ready to raise his hand if he wins at All In.

The Protostar spoke with Tony Schiavone in the ring. Fletcher reminded Okada that what was best for The Family was keeping the gold on him.

As The Protostar turned to calling Konosuke Takeshita a coward, The Alpha arrived to lay Fletcher out and stand tall with the International Championship.

It is good to have Takeshita back after a great run in the G1 Climax for New Japan Pro-Wrestling, and this story is starting to heat up.

At this stage, Fletcher vs. Okada vs. Takeshita does not need any more build to steal the show at All In, but it would be nice to have a big face-off between the three before they fight in Wembley Stadium.

This angle has so much potential, and it is hard to call if Fletcher and Okada can stay on the same page when it matters most.

The Rainmaker is always a menace, but is The Protostar ready to turn face? It may be too soon for that.

Commentary clarified that Callis was on vacation despite all this in-fighting between his family members.

Takeshita and Fletcher moved smoothly through their back-and-forth in full street clothes,

Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay Sit Down with Renee Paquette

Renee Paquette sat down with Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay. They talked about their history, dating back to their shared New Japan Pro-Wrestling history.

The Cleaner questioned The Aerial Assassin's ability to deliver when the lights are brightest.

Ospreay talked up why All In was more important to him than any other moment in his career.

As The Aerial Assassin grew more emotional, The Cleaner played on his emotions, teasing him about how hard it would be on his family (especially his son) if Ospreay lost.

Ospreay and Omega have made the most of their mic time together so far, and this was no different.

In particular, this was the best The Cleaner has sold why fans should hate him when the two collide at All In.

His cocky attitude throughout made clear that Omega is done treating Ospreay as a friend after all they have been through.

This went long for a pre-taped segment in front of a live audience, but it certainly sold more reasons to buy into All In's biggest match.

With one week to go, next week should be the moment Omega and Ospreay get physical.

Omega was nasty at moments when talking to Ospreay, clearly playing more heel despite likely staying babyface after Wembley.

The two argued over their experiences with COVID-19, which was interesting since so many avoid ever talking about the pandemic era.

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

TBS Championship: Maya World (c) vs. Kris Statlander vs. Hikaru Shida vs. Persephone

Last Time in Action: Maya World alongside Thunder Rosa defeated Hikaru Shida and Persephone, and Kris Statlander defeated Viva Van (Dynamite, August 12).

The action was hard hitting and fast paced. Both Shida and Persephone enjoyed hurting their opponents into the commercial break despite issues with one another early.

Shida took over the ring, setting up Persephone to Spear Stat. The Shining Samurai then laid out Maya with a Running Knee.

As Persephone and Shida exchanged blows, Stat returned to lay out Shida. She caught Persephone with a pin, but Maya broke it up with a Senton.

Maya then rolled up Stat to retain her TBS Championship.

Two of the greats of AEW's women's division collided with CMLL's ace and a woman that keeps working to prove herself each week.

It was a recipe for success with non-stop action throughout. The ending was sudden, lacking drama, but that was just because the women could have used a couple more minutes.

For what time they had, Maya looked great while Persephone especially continued to sell herself as a real threat to anyone in the women's division.

Maya needed to win as her title reign is still fresh, though it is hard to call what she will do at All In. Hopefully, she will not be forgotten.

If the TBS Championship is not defended at All In, this Fatal Four Way will look like a missed opportunity that could have been saved for the pay-per-view.

Maya def. Stat, Shida and Persephone by pinfall to retain the TBS Championship.

By the end of the night, the anticipation for what All In was set to deliver was high.

Even if the action was only good rather than great minus Jon Moxley vs. "Switchblade" Jay White, the story build was on point.

This could have been a worthy go-home show for All In. Instead, next week will need to deliver even more crazy action and wild moments for the big show to come.

Will Ospreay and Kenny Omega battled The Don Callis Family in separate trios matches. Maya World defended the TBS Championship against Hikaru Shida, Kris Statlander and Persephone.
The Continental Challenge Cup continued with Jon Moxley vs. "Switchblade" Jay White and Nigel McGuinness vs. Hechicero.

Commentary clarified that Callis was on vacation despite all this in-fighting between his family members.
Takeshita and Fletcher moved smoothly through their back-and-forth in full street clothes,

The Cleaner questioned The Aerial Assassin's ability to deliver when the lights are brightest.
Ospreay talked up why All In was more important to him than any other moment in his career.
As The Aerial Assassin grew more emotional, The Cleaner played on his emotions, teasing him about how hard it would be on his family (especially his son) if Ospreay lost.
Ospreay and Omega have made the most of their mic time together so far, and this was no different.
In particular, this was the best The Cleaner has sold why fans should hate him when the two collide at All In.
His cocky attitude throughout made clear that Omega is done treating Ospreay as a friend after all they have been through.
This went long for a pre-taped segment in front of a live audience, but it certainly sold more reasons to buy into All In's biggest match.
With one week to go, next week should be the moment Omega and Ospreay get physical.
Omega was nasty at moments when talking to Ospreay, clearly playing more heel despite likely staying babyface after Wembley.
The two argued over their experiences with COVID-19, which was interesting since so many avoid ever talking about the pandemic era.

articles.title: Backstage WWE and AEW Rumors on Roman Reigns, Ruby Soho and More
articles.summary: Roman Reigns continues to draw some of the biggest reactions of any WWE Superstar on the roster, but how is he viewed from a character standpoint behind the scenes?
articles.body:
Roman Reigns continues to draw some of the biggest reactions of any WWE Superstar on the roster, but how is he viewed from a character standpoint behind the scenes?

The answer to that question headlines this collection of pro wrestling rumors, featuring reports from the most trusted insiders, also including the in-ring status of Ruby Soho and more.

World heavyweight champion Roman Reigns receives deafening reactions when he enters the arena on Monday nights, but that is not always reflective of the character that appears on WWE Raw.

The Tribal Chief is an egotistical narcissist who has managed to again insulate himself with The Bloodline, forming a shield around himself with his family—the same family he has openly gaslit to get what he wants from them.

False Finish reported that Reigns is listed as a heel by WWE Creative internally.

That is in line with the manner in which he has been booked of late. The way he talked down to, berated and belittled Solo Sikoa on the most recent episode of Raw before getting his comeuppance certainly felt like the actions of a villain.

Hopefully, the idea that Reigns is a heel in the eyes of WWE officials will only help improve this third chapter of the Bloodline, which has struggled to make the same impact as the original incarnation, which can be attributed to creative inconsistencies and too much ambiguity.

Ruby Soho has not wrestled a match for All Elite Wrestling since February 7, 2024, when she teamed with Saraya in a losing effort against Kris Statlander and Willow Nightingale during a taping of Rampage.

Since then, she has given birth to a child and opened a cafe called Victory Road with her partner, Angelo Parker. Amid all of the major life changes, there has been little update on her AEW status or a potential return to the squared circle...until now.

Sean Ross Sapp of Fightful Select reported: "Fightful Select sources are told that Ruby Soho was actually at the AEW tapings in Cincinnati way back in June. We were also told that Ruby was getting clearances from AEW medical for her eventual return to the ring."

He added: "We did hear that some ideas had been floated around for Ruby over the past number of months, but have not learned of anything solid being enacted. Ruby has not been a regular backstage at AEW, either."

While there is no clear indication she will be back any time soon, Sapp's report should be considered a "win" for Soho's fans, who have not heard much from or about the star of late.

If she does return to the squared circle, she will return to an AEW women's division that is much different from the one she last encountered over two years ago.

False Finish also reported WWE Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio pushed for El Fiscal's inclusion in the tournament to crown a No. 1 contender to Roman Reigns' World Heavyweight Championship.

El Fiscal squared off against Rey Fenix Monday night on Raw. Ultimately, he lost to the AAA cruiserweight champion, but he delivered a solid performance that may result in more exposure in the coming weeks and months.

Mysterio is a tremendous ambassador for lucha libre and the talent in AAA. He is a general manager on the screen, but if there is anyone who can influence the power players backstage and get more TV exposure for the young stars tearing it up in Mexico, it is The Master of the 619.

El Fiscal, 26, is the son of legendary luchador Abismo Negro.
paragraphs: Roman Reigns continues to draw some of the biggest reactions of any WWE Superstar on the roster, but how is he viewed from a character standpoint behind the scenes?
The answer to that question headlines this collection of pro wrestling rumors, featuring reports from the most trusted insiders, also including the in-ring status of Ruby Soho and more.
World heavyweight champion Roman Reigns receives deafening reactions when he enters the arena on Monday nights, but that is not always reflective of the character that appears on WWE Raw.

The Tribal Chief is an egotistical narcissist who has managed to again insulate himself with The Bloodline, forming a shield around himself with his family—the same family he has openly gaslit to get what he wants from them.
False Finish reported that Reigns is listed as a heel by WWE Creative internally.

That is in line with the manner in which he has been booked of late. The way he talked down to, berated and belittled Solo Sikoa on the most recent episode of Raw before getting his comeuppance certainly felt like the actions of a villain.

Hopefully, the idea that Reigns is a heel in the eyes of WWE officials will only help improve this third chapter of the Bloodline, which has struggled to make the same impact as the original incarnation, which can be attributed to creative inconsistencies and too much ambiguity.

articles.title: Ilja Dragunov's WWE Future Revealed in New Rumors After Former U.S. Champion's Contract Expired
articles.summary: Following an extended absence from WWE programming, former United States champion Ilja Dragunov is reportedly leaving the company.
articles.body:
Following an extended absence from WWE programming, former United States champion Ilja Dragunov is reportedly leaving the company.

According to PWInsider.com (h/t WrestlePurists ), Dragunov's departure comes amid the expiration of his WWE contract.

False Finish reported that WWE "would have liked Dragunov to stay with the company," but Dragunov made the decision to let his contract expire.

ESPN Addresses 'Completely False' Rumors About Future WWE Contract

After news of Dragunov exiting WWE broke, AEW international champion Kyle Fletcher acknowledged it by posting a photo from a match he had against Dragunov in 2019:

Born in Russia and raised in Germany, the 32-year-old Dragunov became a fixture in NXT UK after initially signing with WWE in 2019.

After a nearly yearlong reign as NXT United Kingdom champion, Dragunov made the move to NXT in 2022. He held the NXT Championship for over 200 days and had memorable rivalries with the likes of Trick Williams, Carmelo Hayes and Bron Breakker.

Dragunov got called up to WWE's main roster in 2024, but it wasn't long before he suffered a torn ACL, which kept him out of action for over a year.

On the Oct. 17 episode of SmackDown, Dragunov made his return to WWE programming as a surprise challenger for the United States Championship, and he beat Sami Zayn for the U.S. title on that night.

About two months later, Dragunov dropped the title to Hayes, and he struggled to secure consistent television time after that.

Dragunov lost a U.S. title rematch against Hayes in March, and then he made his final appearance on WWE programming about a month later when he competed in the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal.

Many fans questioned where Dragunov had been for the past four months, and they now know that his WWE tenure has come to an end, making him a free agent who could be highly sought after on the open market.

As the second-biggest wrestling promotion in the world, AEW stands out as a potential landing spot for Dragunov.

AEW is staging its biggest pay-per-view of the year, All In, at Wembley Stadium in London on Aug. 30, and Dragunov stands out as a strong candidate to be a surprise entrant in the Casino Gauntlet match for a future AEW World Championship opportunity should he sign with the company.

New Japan Pro-Wrestling could also be a great fit for Dragunov's hard-hitting wrestling style, while TNA would potentially provide him with a chance to be a world title contender and main eventer immediately upon signing.

Regardless of where he ends up, Dragunov should have little issue landing on his feet and making a major impact in the pro wrestling world.

articles.title: Islanders Reveal 3rd Jersey Design Contest Winner From Fan Vote Bracket in Videos
articles.summary: The New York Islanders unveiled the team's third jersey design for the 2026-27 season on Thursday.
articles.body:
The New York Islanders unveiled the team's third jersey design for the 2026-27 season on Thursday.

After fans voted for the Islanders' new jersey, they revealed that the "Navy Lighthouse" design concept was selected as the winner.

Fans will also have an opportunity to provide input on the final jersey design, as Thursday's concept contained a navy blue jersey featuring a lighthouse logo with orange and teal stripes on the sleeves.

New York is looking to end a brief two-year playoff drought during its 2026-27 campaign after wrapping up a 43-34-5 finish last season.

articles.title: Australian Darts Masters: James Wade dominates tournament opener as Ross Smith stunned by Brody Klinge in Wollongong
articles.summary: James Wade thrashed Tim Pusey 6-0 in the opening round of the Australian Darts Masters; Gian van Veen, Stephen Bunting, Josh Rock, Jonny Clayton and Gerwyn Price all made winning starts as Ross Smith made a shock early exit
articles.body:
Brody Klinge set up a quarter-final showdown against Gian van Veen at the KenoGo Australian Darts Masters after a shock victory over Ross Smith in Wollongong.

Klinge was the solitary Oceanic representative to triumph on a terrific opening day at the WIN Entertainment Centre, registering an 11-dart break to sink Ross Smith in a deciding-leg epic.

Smith crashed in eight maximums during a captivating affair, although he was punished for squandering two match darts in the decider, as Klinge celebrated the biggest victory of his career.

  • Australian Darts Masters: Latest schedule
  • Darts in 2026: Key dates, calendar, results 📅
  • Got Sky? Watch on the Sky Sports app 📱
  • Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW 📺

"I'm over the moon with that," said Klinge, who averaged 96 to Smith's 102.88. "That was the adrenaline rush of my life. I felt a lot more comfortable playing this time around and it showed in my performance I think.

"Ross was throwing everything at me. I was lucky he missed at the end there, but I took my chance. I'm on a free rein now. I'm just going to do my best and keep going. There's no pressure on me."

Klinge's reward is a tussle against Van Veen on Finals Day, after the world No 2 conjured up a spectacular 161 checkout to wrap up a clinical 6-3 success against Raymond Smith.

However, the performance of the night was produced by James Wade, who averaged 112.73 - the second-highest recorded in a World Series of Darts event in Australia - during a six-leg demolition of Tim Pusey.

"That felt amazing. Everything just fell into my hands there," admitted Wade, who closed out victory with a 164 finish and will play Stephen Bunting in the quarter-finals.

"I think I'm guilty of sometimes forgetting how lucky I am to do what I do, but I'm just happy to be here and I'm playing alright. If I replicate that level tomorrow everyone is stuffed, but tomorrow is a different day!"

2024 champion Gerwyn Price will face Josh Rock in a fascinating last-eight showdown on Saturday, having reeled off four consecutive legs - including back-to-back 124 and 108 checkouts - in a 6-2 victory over Simon Whitlock.

Rock also won four straight legs to seal a 6-3 success against Adam Leek, while Jonny Clayton will go head-to-head with Australian No 1 Damon Heta after opening his bid for back-to-back World Series titles with a hard-fought 6-3 victory against Ben Robb.

Heta averaged 102.39 in his 6-2 thumping of fellow countryman Joe Comito, while the other tie saw Stephen Bunting fight back from trailing 3-0 to beat Mal Cuming 6-3.

The 2026 Australian Darts Masters will reach its climax with the quarter-finals, semi-finals and final during a blockbuster evening session at the WIN Entertainment Centre on Saturday.

articles.title: Australian Darts Masters: James Wade claims first-ever World Series of Darts title with victory over home favourite Brody Klinge
articles.summary: James Wade ended the fairytale run of Brody Klinge at the Australian Darts Masters to claim a maiden World Series of Darts crown; Klinge had beaten Ross Smith, Gian van Veen and New Zealand champion Jonny Clayton en route to the final
articles.body:
James Wade claimed a maiden World Series of Darts crown with an 8-5 victory over home favourite Brody Klinge at the KenoGo Australian Darts Masters in Wollongong.

The 43-year-old started off his KenoGo Australian Darts Masters with a 6-0 whitewash of Tim Pusey on Friday and declared that everyone was "stuffed" if he repeated the same form on Saturday.

Wade averaged 112.73 - the second-highest recorded in a World Series of Darts event in Australia - during the six-leg demolition of Pusey and entered Saturday playing with confidence and a joy that, he admitted himself after that win, is sometimes lacking for him.

  • Darts in 2026: Key dates, calendar, results 📅
  • Got Sky? Watch on the Sky Sports app 📱
  • Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW 📺

"It's been a while since I've won something," quipped Wade, who last tasted success in a televised event at the 2021 UK Open.

"My children always say to me: 'Daddy can you get a trophy'? I have to keep buying them!

"It's fantastic. I really enjoyed myself this weekend. I'm absolutely made up, and to win the title in Australia is even better.

"I'd like to say a massive well done to Brody.

"I had to graft and work really hard, and I'll be really disappointed if he doesn't pursue what he's doing."

Although there were no more whitewashes, the fantastic darts continued on Saturday at the WIN Entertainment Centre. After accounting for Stephen Bunting in his quarter-final clash, he crashed in eight maximums as he beat Gerwyn Price 7-4 in the semi-final to set up the showdown with the home favourite.

As for Klinge, he may have come up short in the final but can be proud of his run, which started with a massive shock on Friday as he registered an 11-dart break to eliminate Ross Smith in a deciding leg after 'Smudger' squandered two match darts.

Fresh from the biggest win of his career, Klinge then beat Gian van Veen 6-4 in the quarter-final and Jonny Clayton, who was aiming to claim back-to-back titles after his win in New Zealand, 7-5.

In the final though, he came up against a rejuvenated Wade and was two legs down heading into the interval despite both players averaging 107.

A fine 140 finish kept him in it at 6-4, but 'The Machine' kept his composure and overcame the boos of the partisan home crowd finishing double tops, and double 10 after Klinge failed to check out on 60.

Although the fairytale came to an end, the tournament performance is one that the Australian reflected on very positively.

"It's been absolutely amazing," revealed Klinge, who averaged 104.56 in defeat.

"The crowd have been behind me the whole time and I've really enjoyed the whole experience. I cannot believe I got here.

"Every opportunity that comes my way I'll try and take it. I'm going to keep playing and see what happens."

articles.title: New WWE Backstage Rumors on Lil Yachty as Fans Rip Triple H over Debut Match vs. Baron Corbin
articles.summary: Ahead of his WWE debut match against Baron Corbin on Sunday Night's Main Event on Sept. 6, rapper Lil Yachty has reportedly impressed with his work ethic.
articles.body:
Ahead of his WWE debut match against Baron Corbin on Sunday Night's Main Event on Sept. 6, rapper Lil Yachty has reportedly impressed with his work ethic.

According to False Finish , Yachty has "earned the respect of many within the company and industry" for taking his role in WWE seriously and dedicating himself to it.

False Finish added that Yachty has been training at the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida, in preparation for his match against Corbin, and the plan is for him to remain on WWE programming "for the foreseeable future."

WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before Heatwave 2026

Many wrestling fans haven't been quite so accepting of Yachty's presence on WWE TV or his upcoming match, as Triple H's post on X about Yachty vs. Corbin was met with a deluge of negative comments:

Despite that, WWE is moving forward with it, and the match figures to be a central part of the rivalry between Corbin and Trick Williams.

Williams dropped the United States Championship to Corbin at SummerSlam after getting distracted by Corbin putting Yachty through a table.

Trick has been trying to get a rematch since then, and during a segment on Friday night's episode of SmackDown, Yachty got some licks in on Corbin with his "Trick Stick" kendo stick.

A furious Corbin agreed to give Williams a U.S. title opportunity, but it came with a major condition.

Corbin first stipulated that he would get to face Yachty at Sunday Night's Main Event. If Yachty can last five minutes without losing, then Trick will get his rematch, but if Corbin wins within five minutes, then Williams won't get another title shot.

The match will take place in Yachty's hometown of Atlanta, which suggests he may have a lot more fan support than he might have in a different location.

Many celebrities have had matches over the years and earned the respect of fans who went into it with skepticism. Yachty will have a chance to do that as well at Sunday Night's Main Event, but it sounds like he is already respected by those behind the scenes in WWE.

articles.title: Fallon Sherrock sweeps aside Lisa Ashton 5-0 to claim her first Women's Series title of 2026
articles.summary: Fallon Sherrock denies Lisa Ashton a second title of the day at Leicester's Mattioli Arena with a rampant 5-0 win  to scoop her first Women's Series title in over 16 months; Beau Greaves - absent from Saturday's action - remains on top of the rankings
articles.body:
Lisa Ashton and Fallon Sherrock shared the spoils at Events 17-18 of the PDC Women’s Series on Saturday, as the duo scooped a title each to reinforce their positions of second and third in the rankings respectively.

Leicester's Mattioli Arena played host to a double-header of Women's Series action, with Ashton and Sherrock celebrating success in Event 17 and 18.

Ashton stormed to the Event 17 crown, breezing to the last 16 with a trio of whitewash victories, before conceding just a solitary leg against Lauren Hall to reach the quarter-finals.

articles.title: Beau Greaves: 'Beau and Arrow' defeats Lisa Ashton and Aileen de Graaf to close in on her 60th title on the Women's Series circuit
articles.summary: After missing out on Saturday's action, darting sensation Beau Greaves returns to the Women's Series with a bang as the Doncaster star wins back-to-back titles on Sunday to claim her 58th and 59th titles on the Women's Series circuit
articles.body:
Beau Greaves defeated Lisa Ashton and Aileen de Graaf on Sunday to close in on her 60th title on the Women's Series circuit.

Sunday's Women's Series double-header saw Events 19 and 20 take place at the Matiolli Arena, as Greaves returned to winning ways on the circuit after missing yesterday's action.

Greaves opened her account Sunday morning with three consecutive whitewash victories over Jane Hawtin, Sue Lowther and Vicky Pruim respectively,

  • Darts in 2026: Key dates, calendar, results 📅
  • Got Sky? Watch on the Sky Sports app 📱
  • Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW 📺

The 22-year-old was almost denied a 58th Women's Series title, as she fought back from 3-2 down to beat Gemma Hayter to book her spot in the quarter-final stage.

Greaves raced into the semi-final, as she beat Aileen de Graaf 5-1 with an average of over 96, before booking her place in the Event 19 showpiece as she raced past Kirsty Hutchinson 5-2.

In a repeat bout of the 2025 Women's World Matchplay semi-final between 'Beau 'n' Arrow' and Lisa Ashton, it was Greaves' who came out victor in the final as she beat Ashton 5-3.

Despite dropping the opening leg in the final, Greaves responded with three legs of her own in quick succession to gain a two-leg advantage on Ashton, before sealing the victory with a brilliant 14-dart leg.

Greaves opened her Event 20 campaign in the same manner as she did earlier in the day, winning back-to-back matches in quick succession, beating Leanne Halls and Felicia Bay 4-0.

The Doncaster star - who only dropped three legs in the entire event - won consecutive matches 4-1 over Louise Pearson and Rhian O'Sullivan respectively, before dispatching Angela Kirkwood 5-0 to seal her spot in the final four.

There, she raced into the final, as Greaves beat Karolina Ratajska 5-1, opening her account in that match with a brilliant 11-dart leg.

De Graaf's below-par performance in the final meant that Greaves was victorious once again and claimed her 59th Women's Series, averaging upwards of 91 and whitewashing the Dutchwoman.

Greaves remains on top of the Women's Series rankings, with Ashton and Sherrock solidifying their positions in second and third respectively, as Hayter sits just behind the pair in fourth spot and in the final qualification spot for the 2026/27 World Darts Championship.
