articles.title: BS Meter on Dylan Larkin, Cutter Gauthier and the Latest NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: The dog days of the NHL off-season continue as August draws to a close.
articles.body:
The dog days of the NHL off-season continue as August draws to a close.

Following a frenzy of activity in the trade market within the first two days of July, business has slowed to a crawl. Only five trades have occurred since July 2 , all involving minor-league players.

However, trade activity could pick up once the calendar flips to September. With training camps opening in mid-month and the regular season beginning on Sept. 29 , NHL general managers could soon start shopping around to address any lingering roster issues.

Meanwhile, the media rumor mill continues churning over potential moves involving some key players.

Some, such as Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin, have previously surfaced in trade rumors this summer. Others, like Calgary Flames defenseman Zach Whitecloud, have started popping up as trade candidates.

Follow along as we dust off our BS Meter to separate fact from fiction regarding the latest NHL trade chatter.

Montréal Canadiens Have 2 'Sign-and-Trade' Candidates

With September and the start of training camp fast approaching, the Montréal Canadiens have not yet re-signed defenseman Arber Xhekaj and winger Zachary Bolduc. The two depth players are restricted free agents coming off low-cost contracts and should be affordable re-signings for the Canadiens.

Stu Cowan of The Montreal Gazette speculated about whether Xhekaj and Bolduc still have futures with the Canadiens. Because they haven't re-signed yet, he concluded that they could be part of a sign-and-trade scenario.

The Canadiens still require a second-line center. Cowan pointed out that general manager Kent Hughes hasn't ruled out making a trade in September or October, adding that he wouldn't make a "dumb trade" for a quick fix.

Given the young talent within the Canadiens system, there might not be room for Xhekaj and Bolduc. They could be pushed out if one or two of their promising players crack the lineup during training camp.

Sign-and-trade scenarios usually happen with stars or second-tier talent, not low-cost depth players. Both could draw attention if available in the trade market. However, even in a package deal, they won't fetch the second-line center the Canadiens require without adding a significant sweetener.

Darcy Kuemper and Trevor Moore Could Be Los Angeles Kings' Trade Candidates

The Los Angeles Kings made several roster changes during this offseason.

Long-time captain Anze Kopitar retired, and Andrei Kuzmenko and Mathieu Joseph departed via free agency. Mats Zuccarello and Erik Haula arrived via free agency. So did Corey Perry, back for a second stint after joining them last season.

Nevertheless, Kings general manager Ken Holland might not be done tinkering with his lineup this season. Ryan O'Hara of The Hockey News suggested goaltender Darcy Kuemper and winger Trevor Moore as trade candidates .

Kuemper, 36, was a Vezina Trophy finalist with the Kings in 2024-25. However, he struggled last season after an injury, which cost him the starter's job to Anton Forsberg. If he can't regain that spot, the Kings might attempt to move him and his $5.3 million cap hit .

O'Hara complimented Moore's speed and ability, but noted the 31-year-old winger hasn't cracked the Kings' top-six forward lines full-time. He carries a $4.2 million annual cap hit through 2027-28 , and scored a career-high 31 goals in 2022-23.

Both players could be trade chips to address other roster issues for the Kings. Kuemper could draw interest from teams seeking an experienced starting goalie, while Moore could entice clubs that are in the market for a skillful middle-six winger.

Calgary Flames Could Trade Zach Whitecloud

The Calgary Flames have rebuilt their roster over the last two seasons by trading veterans for draft picks, prospects, and younger players.

They're expected to be sellers this season if they're out of playoff contention by the March 1 trade deadline.

Zach Whitecloud is currently the Flames' biggest trade chip. Acquired from the Vegas Golden Knights in January, the 29-year-old is a reliable defenseman with Stanley Cup experience. He has two years left on his contract with an affordable AAV of $2.8 million.

Kent Wilson of the Calgary Sun believes the Flames will retain Whitecloud this season to provide experience and leadership to their young defense corps. However, he doesn't rule out a trade if young blueliners Simon Nemec and Zayne Parekh step up this season.

Some observers still consider Whitecloud a suitable trade target this summer for clubs seeking a skillful, experienced top-four defenseman with a right-handed shot. The Toronto Maple Leafs and Montreal Canadiens have been suggested as suitors.

The Flames could move Whitecloud if their young defensemen show improvement this season. However, those promising youngsters will likely need another season to develop, meaning they'll need a seasoned hand like Whitecloud to help them.

Anaheim Ducks Could Make Cost-Cutting Trade to Sign Cutter Gauthier

The Anaheim Ducks were caught by surprise when center Leo Carlsson signed a five-year contract offer with the Philadelphia Flyers worth an average annual value of $18 million.

The Ducks matched the offer, but it left them with insufficient salary cap space to re-sign Cutter Gauthier.

A restricted free agent coming off an entry-level contract, Gauthier led the Ducks last season with 41 goals and 69 points. The 21-year-old winger reportedly rejected a four-year contract offer from the Ducks worth $14 million annually.

With $9.07 million in salary cap space , the Ducks must shed salary once Gauthier is signed. They'll get some short-term salary-cap relief by placing sidelined winger Troy Terry ($7 million AAV) on long-term injury reserve, but they must be cap-compliant when he's ready to return to the lineup.

Andre Leal of The Hockey News believes the Ducks must make a couple of cost-cutting trades . He suggested wingers Alex Killorn ($6.25 million AAV), Chris Kreider ($6.5 million), and Frank Vatrano ($4.6 million) as likely trade candidates.

If Gauthier has rejected $14 million annually, he won't accept anything within the Ducks' current remaining cap space. The Ducks are a rising team in the Western Conference and cannot afford to lose their leading goal scorer. Killorn, Kreider or Vatrano could be playing elsewhere later this season.

Minnesota Wild Can't Afford to Acquire Dylan Larkin

In early June, it was first reported that Dylan Larkin requested a trade. That made the 30-year-old Detroit Red Wings center a fixture in the rumor mill and appeared in our August NHL Trade Targets list.

Larkin has a full no-movement clause, but is reportedly willing to waive it for the Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Florida Panthers, and Dallas Stars.

According to MLive.com's Ansar Khan, the Wild were his preferred landing spot , but they might be unable to meet the Wings' asking price.

Khan stated the Red Wings sought, at minimum, a top-six forward (preferably a center) in return for Larkin. However, the Wild aren't parting with that type of asset, and Khan indicated the Red Wings aren't interested in a return of futures such as draft picks and prospects.

Wild followers aren't optimistic about their club's chances of landing Larkin. In a fan poll earlier this month by Michael Russo and Joe Smith of The Athletic, 68 percent of respondents didn't believe their team could acquire him, citing the club's limited trade capital.

The Wild don't have a top-six forward to spare, and their lack of a true first-line center is the reason they were linked to Larkin in the first place. Unless the Wings lower their price, the Wild must get creative, perhaps by getting a third team involved that has the assets that could interest Detroit.

Stats via NHL.com , salary cap and contract info via PuckPedia .

articles.title: Ranking the 5 Most Likely Men's WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Winners
articles.summary: Sunday Night's Main Event is the next big show for WWE on September 6, but the next official premium live event is Money in the Bank on October 10.
articles.body:
Sunday Night's Main Event is the next big show for WWE on September 6, but the next official premium live event is Money in the Bank on October 10.

The MITB event is usually one of the more anticipated PLEs on the calendar because the outcome isn't always as predictable as the average match. Plus, who doesn't love a good fight with ladders?

There are a lot of potential names who could end up in this year's men's Money in the Bank bout, but only a handful seem like possible winners.

Let's take a look at some of the most likely names to walk out of New Orleans with the briefcase.

Royce Keys has had slightly inconsistent booking lately, but it's clear WWE management sees him as a potential top star.

He might be new to the company, but the 17-year veteran is by no means a rookie, so it would make perfect sense for him to end up in this match.

The only thing that kept us from placing him higher on the list is the fact that he has not won a title in WWE yet, and it might be best to give him a run with the United States or Intercontinental Championship to see how he does.

Keys winning would immediately inject some new blood into the main event scene, which WWE sorely needs right now.

Finn Balor has talked a lot about wanting to get back into the hunt for a world title since coming to SmackDown, and this might be his way back into the chase.

Balor was the first-ever universal champion, but an injury during the title match in which he won the belt forced him to relinquish it before he ever got to defend it.

Now that he is free from The Judgment Day and back to his old babyface ways, it would be the perfect time to throw him into the title picture.

His popularity has been consistent, and Balor has always been a reliable performer in the ring, so there would be no downside to giving him the briefcase at this stage in his career.

Drew McIntyre has been out of action since losing to Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania 42, but if he is ready to come back, this would be the perfect time.

The MITB briefcase would make him even more dangerous than he already is, which is saying a lot because he is one of the most physically imposing members on the WWE roster.

Whether the Scot does it as a heel or babyface doesn't matter because his return would be cheered by fans either way, so WWE has some wiggle room with the kind of story it would tell with him holding the case.

The only downside to this scenario is that McIntyre won the briefcase in 2024, so having him repeat so soon might not be the best option.

WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before Heatwave 2026

Trick Williams is currently involved in a feud with Baron Corbin over the United States Championship, but once that is done, it wouldn't be surprising to see WWE test him out in the main event scene.

It's no secret that WWE sees Trick as a valued member of the roster. He is booked strong, featured regularly and has a celebrity manager. His ascension has been quick but steady.

Putting the MITB briefcase in his hands would not be a bad idea at all. Even if he didn't successfully cash it in, having him circling the world title picture would be a great next step in his career.

If he ends up being booked in the match, we're giving him strong odds to win.

Solo Sikoa is definitely going to end up challenging Roman Reigns for the world title at some point, but he would be so much more dangerous with the MITB briefcase.

This would be a slam-dunk decision for WWE. Sikoa has built real momentum with the WWE Universe in recent months, and now is the time to capitalize.

Having him use the briefcase to defeat Reigns would also protect The Tribal Chief's character, which is something WWE seems intent on doing.

A few months of Sikoa parading around with the briefcase and taunting his cousin with it before finally cashing it in would be highly entertaining television.

Do we actually think Danhausen will win the Money in the Bank match? No, but there is an argument for why it would be great.

The beauty of his character is he is not driven by the same motivations as every other pro wrestler. Titles don't seem to be his top priority, so there is an easy comedic avenue to take.

Imagine Danhausen wins the case and then opens it to find a contract when he was expecting human monies. He would be the first person in WWE history to be mad about winning, but he could take advantage of the situation.

Having him attempt to auction the case off to the highest bidder would make for some hilarious segments, especially if someone unexpected ends up getting the case in the end.

Or, Danhausen could place a curse on the case so that whoever tried to cash it in fails miserably. There are multiple options for how to make this work.

This might not be the kind of decision every fan would enjoy, but if you like Danhausen, you would probably enjoy him running around with the briefcase for a while.

articles.title: Bayley Fuels WWE Rumors, New Reports on Joe Hendry and Ilja Dragunov's Exit amid AEW Buzz
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Bayley Has Exchange with Pearce Amid WWE Absence

ESPN Addresses 'Completely False' Rumors About Future WWE Contract

Bayley has not been seen on WWE programming since last month, but she got fans talking Sunday after an exchange with Raw general manager Adam Pearce.

In response to an Instagram post (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News) by Bayley about her 10-year anniversary of getting called up to WWE's main roster, Pearce commented with clapping hands emojis.

Bayley responded by writing, "Hey, let's talk," to which Pearce replied, "You know where to find me."

The last time Bayley appeared on a televised WWE show was on July 18 when she lost to Lyra Valkyria at Saturday Night's Main Event.

She subsequently had two matches at WWE live events, but it has now been over a month since Bayley was part of WWE programming.

Bayley's absence comes amid a great deal of speculation regarding her pro wrestling future.

While the exact end date of Bayley's WWE contract is not publicly known, Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t WrestlingInc.com's Julien D'Alessandro ) reported earlier this month that he had heard her deal is up in January.

As is the case with any big WWE name who may be on the verge of free agency, some have theorized that Bayley could make the jump to AEW to reunite with longtime friend Mercedes Moné.

However, since Bayley's name has been mentioned often on WWE programming as of late, particularly by Valkyria, there is at least some belief that her WWE tenure may not be over yet.

Dave Meltzer of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t Holloway ) recently offered his perspective, saying, "The frequent mentions of her on Raw this week would indicate to me that they expect her back. If they believed she might be leaving, they would not mention her name."

Bayley's exchange with Pearce could potentially be another clue that a return to WWE programming is possible, but anything could be on the table until and unless she resurfaces.

Reported Reason for Hendry's Recent WWE Hiatus

Joe Hendry's absence from WWE programming over the past few weeks is reportedly due to an outside-the-ring project he is working on for the company.

According to PWInsider.com (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), Hendry has a role in a live-action micro-drama for mobile platforms as part of WWE's partnership with ReelShort.

Prior to his hiatus, Hendry took part in a concert with Danhausen on the July 27 episode of Raw. However, they were interrupted and attacked by Judgment Day members Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh, as well as boxer Ryan Garcia.

At SummerSlam, Hendry showed up during the Human Monies on a Pole match between Danhausen and Mysterio, and he helped Danhausen pull off the victory.

The next night on Raw, Hendry lost decisively in a match against Bron Breakker, and he has not shown up on Raw since then.

Hendry was called up to WWE's main roster in April following a successful run in NXT that saw him hold the NXT Championship once.

While Hendry has not enjoyed that same level of success on Raw yet, the fact that WWE is using him for outside projects suggests that the company sees plenty of value in his skill set.

Rumors on Dragunov's Future After WWE Departure

Ilja Dragunov is reportedly being linked to AEW following the expiration of his WWE contract.

According to Fightful Select (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), AEW sources have not yet heard about Dragunov joining the company, but other sources within pro wrestling expressed their belief that Dragunov ultimately will sign with AEW based on a "hunch."

PWInsider.com (h/t WrestlePurists ) first reported Saturday that Dragunov's WWE contract was expiring, leading to his exit from the company.

False Finish followed up by reporting that although WWE "would have liked Dragunov to stay with the company," he ultimately made the decision to leave.

Given that Dragunov's contract expired rather than him getting notified of a release, the typical 90-day non-compete clause does not apply to him.

That means Dragunov is a free agent and already free to work elsewhere at any time.

The 32-year-old Dragunov has long been regarded as one of the most physical and entertaining in-ring workers in pro wrestling, which led to some major accolades in WWE.

Dragunov was both an NXT United Kingdom and NXT champion before getting called up to the main roster and holding the United States Championship.

However, Dragunov's screen time took a major hit after he dropped the U.S. title to Carmelo Hayes in December, and he had not been seen on WWE programming since April prior to his departure.

If Dragunov and AEW do have mutual interest, it would perhaps behoove them to get a deal done quickly because he could show up next Sunday at the All In pay-per-view as a surprise entrant in the Casino Gauntlet match.

articles.standfirst: El narrador de TV Azteca fue claro en manifestar sus preferencias televisivas
articles.summary: El narrador de TV Azteca fue claro en manifestar sus preferencias televisivas
articles.body: Muchos medios de Comunicaciones y diversos comentaristas de espectáculos han comentado los supuestos problemas que está teniendo Televisa con el bajo rating de su reality show estelar de ‘La Casa de los Famosos México 2026’ en la que no estaría alcanzando los niveles de audiencia que batieron marcas en las temporadas anteriores, y mas allá de verificar si esta información es o no es cierta, hay algo que quedó más claro que el agua pura este mismo fin de semana y es que el narrador principal de futbol en TV Azteca, Christian Martinoli, no ayudará a que ese niveles lleguen a los objetivos deseados en la televisora que es propiedad de Emilio Azcárraga Jean. Martinoli es visto muchas veces en los aeropuertos, debido a las narraciones que realiza fuera de su residencia en la Ciudad de México, sin embargo, de forma un tanto extraña, esta vez fue captado con una maleta en la Terminal 2 del Aeropuerto Internacional de la Ciudad de México el mismo domingo, donde accedió a mandar un saludo a un fanático que se lo pidió mientras caminaba no tan a prisa como de costumbre. Más adelante se dio una interacción relativamente cómica, pues el fanático le hizo una pregunta que seguramente el compañero de años y años de transmisión del analista Luis García, no esperaba y, sin embargo, con todo y una enorme sonrisa en el rostro, la velocidad de pensamiento para ser fiel a sus valores de nacido en Mar del Plata, Argentina, fue digna del recuerdo: Hay que agregar que, en las primeras tres nominaciones, el narrador especialmente de futbol americano de la NFL junto con Toño de Valdés y Enrique Burak tras la salida de Pepe Segarra, estuvo como candidato a salir de la casa, sin embargo, los votos del público lo salvaron, este domingo tampoco salió, pero además ni si quiera fue parte de la citada nominación.

articles.title: 20 Athletes Whose Career Earnings Would Shock You
articles.summary: NBA veteran James Harden recently made headlines when a new three-year, $97 million deal with the Cavaliers put him on track to break the $500 million mark for career earnings.
articles.body:
NBA veteran James Harden recently made headlines when a new three-year, $97 million deal with the Cavaliers put him on track to break the $500 million mark for career earnings.

That raised an immediate question: Which other athletes have career earnings that would shock the average fan? Off we went to scour the all-time leaderboards at Spotrac to find the answer.

This is a subjective exercise, but if a name immediately comes to mind as handsomely paid relative to his body of work, there's a good chance he isn't featured here since the focus was shock value.

For example, Tobias Harris (NBA), Kirk Cousins (NFL) and Stephen Strasburg (MLB) are prime examples of players whom general sports fans would be quick to associate with massive paydays.

However, the following 20 players should be a genuine shock, including four legendary retired athletes whose surprisingly low figures provide a counterpoint to their highly paid counterparts.

Note: All salary figures reflect all money on the books, including future earnings.

With a new three-year, $97 million contract on the books to return to the Cleveland Cavaliers, James Harden is officially on track to join a short list of NBA players who have earned $500 million by the time the 2028-29 season arrives.

Harden split his age-36 season between the Los Angeles Clippers and Cavaliers last year. He continues to contribute at a high level after averaging 23.6 points and 8.0 assists while knocking down 37.5 percent of his attempts from distance.

He enters the 2026-27 campaign ranked 11th on the NBA's all-time scoring list with 29,339 points in 17 seasons.

The massive five-year, $251 million extension that Bradley Beal signed prior to the 2022-23 season helps prop up his massive career earnings total, but it's still shocking to see that number north of $400 million.

The three-time All-Star peaked at 31.3 points per game during the 2020-21 season, when he also earned his only All-NBA selection as a third-team choice. However, he has never advanced beyond the conference semifinals.

The 33-year-old signed a two-year, $13.2 million deal to return to the Clippers in mid-August, although he's also receiving $19.4 million annually from the Phoenix Suns through 2029-30 after they waived and stretched him in 2025. He played just six games last year before undergoing season-ending surgery to repair a fractured hip.

Danilo Gallinari is perhaps best remembered as the centerpiece whom the New York Knicks sent to the Denver Nuggets in their trade for Carmelo Anthony during the 2010-11 season.

At the time, Gallinari was a 22-year-old in his third NBA season who was averaging 15.9 points per game. By the time the 2015-16 season rolled around, he was the leading scorer (19.5 PPG) for a Nuggets team that finished 33-49.

A three-year, $64.8 million sign-and-trade deal that sent him from the Nuggets to the Los Angeles Clippers in 2017 was the largest individual contract that Gallinari ever signed, but he still managed to eclipse the $200 million mark over his 14-year career.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

After Jakob Poeltl served as a valuable bench piece for the Toronto Raptors during the 2017-18 season (his second year in the NBA), the Raptors traded him to the San Antonio Spurs along with DeMar DeRozan in their blockbuster deal to acquire Kawhi Leonard the following summer.

He spent five seasons with the Spurs before ultimately finding his way back to Toronto in 2023. That summer, he inked a four-year, $78 million deal with the Raptors, and he signed a three-year, $84 million extension two years later.

The 7-footer has been a solid role player, but with career averages of 9.1 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.2 blocks, it is surprising to see he has racked up over $200 million in career earnings.

An NBA champion with both the Los Angeles Lakers (2019-20) and Denver Nuggets (2022-23), Kentavious Caldwell-Pope has carved out a rock-solid career as a three-and-D wing, even with some inconsistency in his shooting.

After spending four seasons each with the Detroit Pistons and Lakers to begin his career, he is set to suit up for his fifth team in the last six years after inking a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the Philadelphia 76ers during the offseason.

A three-year, $66 million contract from the Orlando Magic stands as KCP's largest single payday, but his staggering career earnings have been more about steady production over his 13-year run in the NBA.

The Thunder signed Isaiah Hartenstein to a three-year, $87 million deal prior to the 2024-25 season despite his modest career averages of 6.0 points, 5.6 rebounds and 18.0 minutes per game.

He immediately thrived in an expanded role, averaging 11.2 points, 10.7 rebounds and 1.1 blocks for a Thunder squad that finished 68-14 and won the NBA championship.

Productive bigs don't grow on trees, but a player who has averaged double-digit points only once in his career banking more than $150 million stands out as shocking nevertheless.

Michael Jordan signed an eight-year, $25.7 million deal prior to the 1988-89 season. He made only slightly more than teammates Toni Kukoč ($3.56M), Ron Harper ($3.12M), Scottie Pippen ($2.925M) and Dennis Rodman ($2.5M) with a $3.85 million salary in the final year of that contract in 1995-96.

His Airness re-upped with the Bulls on a one-year, $30.14 million contract the following year, which made him the highest-paid athlete in American sports history at the time. But spending the bulk of his career playing on that modest eight-year deal left Jordan's career earnings below $100 million.

Don't shed too many tears for MJ, though. His net worth stands at an estimated $4.3 billion thanks in large part to his Nike, Hanes and Gatorade deals, along with selling his majority stake in the Charlotte Hornets.

With a 3.93 ERA and 108 ERA+ over 1,852.2 career innings, Aaron Nola has been a staple in the Philadelphia Phillies' rotation for more than a decade after the club took him No. 7 overall in the 2014 draft.

However, Nola has made just one All-Star team during that time while receiving Cy Young votes on four occasions. He peaked at third in the balloting during the 2018 season, when he had a 2.37 ERA and 224 strikeouts in 212.1 innings.

The seven-year, $172 million deal to re-sign him shortly after he hit the open market following the 2023 season accounts for a significant chunk of Nola's career earnings, but that's still a shocking figure for a pitcher who's rarely mentioned among the game's elite.

Thanks to a standout glove and some solid pop for a middle infielder, Marcus Semien has racked up 49.7 WAR over 14 seasons in the majors.

That included a five-year stretch from 2019-23 where his 29.3 WAR trailed only Mookie Betts (30.3) among all players, though he has rarely been considered a bona fide superstar at any point in his career.

Now in the fifth season of a seven-year, $175 million deal, Semien has struggled through the worst season of his career after being traded to the New York Mets last offseason. He is still owed $46 million over the final two seasons of his contract.

A five-year, $86 million deal that was the richest ever for a reliever at the time and the longevity to still be one of the best relievers in baseball at the age of 38 have helped Aroldis Chapman put up the highest career earnings of any relief pitcher.

He has been an All-Star each of the past two seasons since joining the Red Sox, posting a 1.46 ERA with 61 saves in 112 appearances. That puts him in a strong position to surpass the $200 million mark before he calls it a career.

What sort of deal will Mason Miller command once he reaches free agency if he continues to pitch at the elite level he has shown for the San Diego Padres?

As a two-time All-Star who has received Cy Young votes just once in his 15-year career, Nathan Eovaldi is an unlikely inclusion on a list of the highest-paid pitchers in MLB history.

With a 3.91 ERA and 105 ERA+ across 1,835 innings, he has put together a solid big league career. A postseason resume that includes a 9-3 record with a 3.05 ERA, 1.04 WHIP and 82 strikeouts in 79.2 innings does help elevate his profile.

Still, his $185.8 million career earnings will slot in ahead of Randy Johnson ($177.0M) on MLB's all-time leaderboard once his current three-year, $75 million deal is fully paid out.

Cal Ripken Jr. was baseball's "Iron Man" with 2,632 consecutive games played. He was far more than just durable with 3,184 hits, 431 home runs, 1,695 RBI and 95.9 WAR en route to Cooperstown.

Despite a career that stretched from 1981 through 2001, the five-year, $32.5 million extension he signed during the 1992 season was the largest deal he inked during his storied career.

His career earnings put Kyle Tucker's $60 million AAV with the Los Angeles Dodgers into perspective, even if we are comparing players across different eras.

Anže Kopitar spent his entire 20-year career with the Los Angeles Kings before retiring after the 2025-26 season. The two-time Stanley Cup winner will go down as one of the best two-way forwards of his era.

However, it's still surprising to see that he currently stands as the fourth-highest-paid player in NHL history , behind only Alex Ovechkin ($170.7M), Sidney Crosby ($165.7M) and Evgeni Malkin ($151.7M).

Granted, Kopitar is projected to fall to No. 10 on that list by the time the 2030-31 season rolls around and some of the game's current stars continue to climb the career-earnings leaderboard.

A huge 13-year, $98 million deal with the Minnesota Wild serves as the backbone of Ryan Suter's impressive career earnings. A 20-year career helped push that total above the nine-figure mark.

His resume is built more on longevity and durability than top-tier accolades. He played in 1,526 games, but he never won a Stanley Cup and never took home any individual hardware.

He has not formally retired, though he didn't play during the 2025-26 season after his contract was bought out by the Dallas Stars.

When Wayne Gretzky signed his three-year, $25.5 million deal with the Los Angeles Kings, his $8.5 million AAV more than doubled the NHL's previous top earner. However, that still wasn't enough to push his career earnings over $50 million.

He also signed an absurd 21-year personal services contract with the Edmonton Oilers early in his career that was ultimately reworked, but his earnings stretched beyond what he made for his time on the ice.

With an estimated net worth of $250 million , he maximized his earning potential with endorsements from brands like Coca-Cola, Nike and McDonald's.

Between a four-year, $160 million deal from the New York Giants that ultimately ended in his release and a two-year, $88 million contract from the Indianapolis Colts, Daniel Jones has quietly put together a staggering career earnings total.

The No. 6 overall pick in the 2019 draft looked like a star in the making when he threw for 3,027 yards and 24 touchdowns as a rookie, but that ended up being his peak in a Giants uniform.

The Colts plucked him from the scrapheap after he was released by the Giants with a one-year, $14 million deal, and he earned his second major payday thanks to a 3,101-yard, 19-touchdown performance over 13 games before he suffered a right Achilles tear.

The son of Hall of Fame lineman Bruce Matthews and part of a Matthews family tree loaded with football talent, left tackle Jake Matthews went No. 6 overall in the 2014 draft and immediately slotted in as Matt Ryan's blindside protector.

Matthews has started 196 consecutive games over 12 seasons in the NFL, which stands as the longest active streak in the NFL. However, he has made just one Pro Bowl and zero All-Pro teams along the way.

The two-year, $45 million extension he signed in March 2025 stands to push his career earnings above the $200 million mark if he plays out the remainder of his contract.

The Minnesota Vikings selected Brian O'Neill in the second round of the 2018 NFL draft out of Pitt and found a franchise right tackle. He has made 120 starts and earned a pair of Pro Bowl selections over his eight NFL seasons.

An initial five-year, $92.5 million extension followed by a four-year, $96 million deal ahead of the final year of that contract has made him one of the highest-paid linemen in football.

Still, it's surprising to see a right tackle with such a gaudy career earnings total just eight years into his career, especially one that has not received top-tier individual recognition.

Sam Darnold received a four-year, $30.25 million rookie deal as the No. 3 overall pick in the 2018 draft by the New York Jets, but his time in the Big Apple failed to deliver on lofty expectations.

After three seasons with the Jets, capped off by a 2-10 showing in 2020, he spent two years with the Carolina Panthers and one with the San Francisco 49ers before enjoying a career renaissance with the Minnesota Vikings in 2024 with 4,319 yards and 35 touchdowns.

That earned him a massive three-year, $100.5 million deal from the Seattle Seahawks as a free agent in 2025. He put up his second straight 14-3 season in his Seattle debut while leading them to a Super Bowl victory.

With four Super Bowl rings and legendary status, Joe Montana is generally mentioned among the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history.

The four-year, $13 million extension he signed prior to the 1990 season made him the highest-paid player in football at the time, which is a perfect snapshot of just how much quarterback salaries have skyrocketed in the last 35 years.

There were 18 quarterbacks during the 2025 season who earned more than Montana did over the course of his entire 17-year career.
paragraphs: NBA veteran James Harden recently made headlines when a new three-year, $97 million deal with the Cavaliers put him on track to break the $500 million mark for career earnings.
That raised an immediate question: Which other athletes have career earnings that would shock the average fan? Off we went to scour the all-time leaderboards at Spotrac to find the answer.
This is a subjective exercise, but if a name immediately comes to mind as handsomely paid relative to his body of work, there's a good chance he isn't featured here since the focus was shock value.
For example, Tobias Harris (NBA), Kirk Cousins (NFL) and Stephen Strasburg (MLB) are prime examples of players whom general sports fans would be quick to associate with massive paydays.
However, the following 20 players should be a genuine shock, including four legendary retired athletes whose surprisingly low figures provide a counterpoint to their highly paid counterparts.
Note: All salary figures reflect all money on the books, including future earnings.

With a new three-year, $97 million contract on the books to return to the Cleveland Cavaliers, James Harden is officially on track to join a short list of NBA players who have earned $500 million by the time the 2028-29 season arrives.

Harden split his age-36 season between the Los Angeles Clippers and Cavaliers last year. He continues to contribute at a high level after averaging 23.6 points and 8.0 assists while knocking down 37.5 percent of his attempts from distance.
He enters the 2026-27 campaign ranked 11th on the NBA's all-time scoring list with 29,339 points in 17 seasons.

The massive five-year, $251 million extension that Bradley Beal signed prior to the 2022-23 season helps prop up his massive career earnings total, but it's still shocking to see that number north of $400 million.

The three-time All-Star peaked at 31.3 points per game during the 2020-21 season, when he also earned his only All-NBA selection as a third-team choice. However, he has never advanced beyond the conference semifinals.

The 33-year-old signed a two-year, $13.2 million deal to return to the Clippers in mid-August, although he's also receiving $19.4 million annually from the Phoenix Suns through 2029-30 after they waived and stretched him in 2025. He played just six games last year before undergoing season-ending surgery to repair a fractured hip.
Danilo Gallinari is perhaps best remembered as the centerpiece whom the New York Knicks sent to the Denver Nuggets in their trade for Carmelo Anthony during the 2010-11 season.

At the time, Gallinari was a 22-year-old in his third NBA season who was averaging 15.9 points per game. By the time the 2015-16 season rolled around, he was the leading scorer (19.5 PPG) for a Nuggets team that finished 33-49.

A three-year, $64.8 million sign-and-trade deal that sent him from the Nuggets to the Los Angeles Clippers in 2017 was the largest individual contract that Gallinari ever signed, but he still managed to eclipse the $200 million mark over his 14-year career.
Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

After Jakob Poeltl served as a valuable bench piece for the Toronto Raptors during the 2017-18 season (his second year in the NBA), the Raptors traded him to the San Antonio Spurs along with DeMar DeRozan in their blockbuster deal to acquire Kawhi Leonard the following summer.

He spent five seasons with the Spurs before ultimately finding his way back to Toronto in 2023. That summer, he inked a four-year, $78 million deal with the Raptors, and he signed a three-year, $84 million extension two years later.
The 7-footer has been a solid role player, but with career averages of 9.1 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.2 blocks, it is surprising to see he has racked up over $200 million in career earnings.

An NBA champion with both the Los Angeles Lakers (2019-20) and Denver Nuggets (2022-23), Kentavious Caldwell-Pope has carved out a rock-solid career as a three-and-D wing, even with some inconsistency in his shooting.

After spending four seasons each with the Detroit Pistons and Lakers to begin his career, he is set to suit up for his fifth team in the last six years after inking a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the Philadelphia 76ers during the offseason.

A three-year, $66 million contract from the Orlando Magic stands as KCP's largest single payday, but his staggering career earnings have been more about steady production over his 13-year run in the NBA.
The Thunder signed Isaiah Hartenstein to a three-year, $87 million deal prior to the 2024-25 season despite his modest career averages of 6.0 points, 5.6 rebounds and 18.0 minutes per game.
He immediately thrived in an expanded role, averaging 11.2 points, 10.7 rebounds and 1.1 blocks for a Thunder squad that finished 68-14 and won the NBA championship.
Productive bigs don't grow on trees, but a player who has averaged double-digit points only once in his career banking more than $150 million stands out as shocking nevertheless.

Michael Jordan signed an eight-year, $25.7 million deal prior to the 1988-89 season. He made only slightly more than teammates Toni Kukoč ($3.56M), Ron Harper ($3.12M), Scottie Pippen ($2.925M) and Dennis Rodman ($2.5M) with a $3.85 million salary in the final year of that contract in 1995-96.

His Airness re-upped with the Bulls on a one-year, $30.14 million contract the following year, which made him the highest-paid athlete in American sports history at the time. But spending the bulk of his career playing on that modest eight-year deal left Jordan's career earnings below $100 million.

Don't shed too many tears for MJ, though. His net worth stands at an estimated $4.3 billion thanks in large part to his Nike, Hanes and Gatorade deals, along with selling his majority stake in the Charlotte Hornets.

With a 3.93 ERA and 108 ERA+ over 1,852.2 career innings, Aaron Nola has been a staple in the Philadelphia Phillies' rotation for more than a decade after the club took him No. 7 overall in the 2014 draft.

However, Nola has made just one All-Star team during that time while receiving Cy Young votes on four occasions. He peaked at third in the balloting during the 2018 season, when he had a 2.37 ERA and 224 strikeouts in 212.1 innings.

The seven-year, $172 million deal to re-sign him shortly after he hit the open market following the 2023 season accounts for a significant chunk of Nola's career earnings, but that's still a shocking figure for a pitcher who's rarely mentioned among the game's elite.
Thanks to a standout glove and some solid pop for a middle infielder, Marcus Semien has racked up 49.7 WAR over 14 seasons in the majors.

That included a five-year stretch from 2019-23 where his 29.3 WAR trailed only Mookie Betts (30.3) among all players, though he has rarely been considered a bona fide superstar at any point in his career.

Now in the fifth season of a seven-year, $175 million deal, Semien has struggled through the worst season of his career after being traded to the New York Mets last offseason. He is still owed $46 million over the final two seasons of his contract.

A five-year, $86 million deal that was the richest ever for a reliever at the time and the longevity to still be one of the best relievers in baseball at the age of 38 have helped Aroldis Chapman put up the highest career earnings of any relief pitcher.

He has been an All-Star each of the past two seasons since joining the Red Sox, posting a 1.46 ERA with 61 saves in 112 appearances. That puts him in a strong position to surpass the $200 million mark before he calls it a career.
What sort of deal will Mason Miller command once he reaches free agency if he continues to pitch at the elite level he has shown for the San Diego Padres?
As a two-time All-Star who has received Cy Young votes just once in his 15-year career, Nathan Eovaldi is an unlikely inclusion on a list of the highest-paid pitchers in MLB history.

With a 3.91 ERA and 105 ERA+ across 1,835 innings, he has put together a solid big league career. A postseason resume that includes a 9-3 record with a 3.05 ERA, 1.04 WHIP and 82 strikeouts in 79.2 innings does help elevate his profile.
Still, his $185.8 million career earnings will slot in ahead of Randy Johnson ($177.0M) on MLB's all-time leaderboard once his current three-year, $75 million deal is fully paid out.

Despite a career that stretched from 1981 through 2001, the five-year, $32.5 million extension he signed during the 1992 season was the largest deal he inked during his storied career.

articles.title: World Series of Darts Finals: Luke Littler and Michael van Gerwen to headline £450k event as full 32-player field confirmed
articles.summary: A top prize of £100,000 will be up for grabs at the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals, with Luke Littler, Michael van Gerwen and Gerwyn Price set to headline blockbuster 32-player field, with tournament set to commence on September 17
articles.body:
Luke Littler, Michael van Gerwen and Gerwyn Price will headline a packed field competing for a top prize of £100,000 at the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals.

The event, which has a £450,000 prize pot, will return to the AFAS Live in Amsterdam and is set to take place between September 17-20.

Reigning champion Van Gerwen will be out to defend his title on home soil after he bested Littler in last year's final to scoop an £80,000 cheque at last year's event.

  • Darts in 2026: Key dates, calendar, results 📅
  • Got Sky? Watch on the Sky Sports app📱
  • Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW 📺

Van Gerwen has been in excellent form on the circuit this year, having already won the Bahrain Darts Masters in January and the Nordic Darts Masters in June.

He also came close to winning the inaugural Saudi Arabia Darts Masters in January, but was bested by Littler 8-5 in the final.

World Matchplay champion Littler enters the tournament as the third seed, while Price, who was beaten by the 19-year-old in the final at the Winter Gardens in Blackpool, is the second seed.

Luke Humphries also joins the 32-player field as the fourth seed, after he claimed victory at the US Darts masters in June, while New Zealand Darts Masters winner Jonny Clayton and Australian Darts Masters champion James Wade are seeded sixth and seventh, respectively.

Gian van Veen and Stephen Bunting, seeded fifth and eighth, make up the final seeded players on the list.

Those inside the top 24 of the final World Series rankings will gain a berth to play in Amsterdam.

Australian Brody Klinge, who was beaten by Wade in the final of the Australian Darts Masters, will make his debut at the World Series of Darts Finals.

Nathan Aspinall, Josh Rock and Danny Noppert will also join the field, while Ross Smith, who won the Players Championship 20 in June after picking up his maiden European Tour title earlier in the year is also in the field.

Ryan Searle, Wessel Nijman, Chris Dobey and Jermaine Wattimena have also gained tickets to Amsterdam as the four top non-qualified players from the PDC World Rankings as of August 23.

The field was confirmed following Monday night's Tour Card Holder Qualifier in which Rob Cross was among four names to book their place at the World Series of Darts Finals.

Cross bested Dirk van Duijvenbode in Leicester to book his place in Amsterdam, and was joined by Kevin Doets, as well as Karel Sedlacek and Callan Rydz, who will both make their debuts at September's event.

The first round of the tournament will commence over two sessions on Thursday 17 and Friday 18 September, before round two begins on Saturday, September 19.

The finals will then begin on Sunday, September 20, with the quarter-finals set to get under way in the afternoon, before the semi-finals and final later in the evening.

articles.title: The Rock-WrestleMania 43 Speculation and WWE Rumors on Drew McIntyre, Charlotte, Alexa Bliss & SNME
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Even though it's expected the Saudi Arabia government will present several WWE legends with lucrative financial offers to be involved in WrestleMania 43 in some capacity, The Rock's film schedule might prevent him from being part of the event.

While speaking with Variety 's Jack Dunn and Marc Malkin , Vin Diesel said the current plan is to start filming Fast Forever , the final movie in the Fast & Furious franchise, in December.

"We start shooting in December, if I can make good on the request from the studio," Diesel said.

The Rock, who made a cameo appearance in a mid-credits scene at the end of Fast X , is listed in the cast for the new film despite a previous real-life feud with Diesel that played a part in his absence from the eighth and ninth movies.

Steve Carrier of Ringside News noted the filming schedule, particularly for a production of this size, is likely to last months and could stretch into WrestleMania season.

There are variables that could make it so The Rock has a window in his schedule if he wants to be involved at WrestleMania. No one has said the size of his role in the movie, so it's plausible he won't be needed on set for the entire production.

With Saudi Arabia already believed to be paying $250 million to host WrestleMania next year, the expectation is also that the government will present major financial offers to WWE legends to get them on the card in some capacity.

It was previously reported Saudi officials are preparing an offer to The Rock that would be the largest payday ever given to any wrestler to work a single show in the history of the sport.

WWE has dreamed of a Rock-Roman Reigns match for years. The closest it ever got was in 2024 when the Great One appeared on the first Raw of the year to tease a bout with the Tribal Chief that was then scuttled when Cody Rhodes won the Royal Rumble, though The Rock did wrestle on the show in a tag match.

If The Rock is going to do another match, one would assume he would want it to be sooner than later given that he will turn 55 on May 2 and it requires a lot of physical training to keep his body in the shape to be The Rock everyone thinks of in a WWE ring.

WWE Figuring Out Drew McIntyre's Return Storyline

Having been off WWE television since WrestleMania to work on various outside projects, Drew McIntyre is now waiting for creative to find a story to get him back in the ring.

Per PWInsider Elite (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News), McIntyre is back in the United States after completing work on his other commitments, but WWE's creative team hasn't started plotting out his return at this point.

McIntyre lost to Jacob Fatu in an unsanctioned match at WrestleMania 42. The bout was done to write the Scottish Warrior off television for the time being due to being cast in the Highlander reboot and the Russell Crowe-starring The Last Druid .

The Last Druid started filming in Spain in June. Crowe posted a picture with McIntyre on Instagram on Aug. 5, writing they had recently finished filming.

One thing potentially holding up McIntyre's return is all of the people he was feuding with prior to leaving are embroiled in storylines right now. His last two opponents prior to Fatu were Sami Zayn and Cody Rhodes over the undisputed title.

The decision also has to be made if McIntyre will return as a heel or babyface. If he is staying on SmackDown, it might be better to bring him back as a babyface since they just turned Zayn heel and Randy Orton also returned as a villain.

Of course, the Raw roster also needs an infusion of talent, particularly on the heel side. Roman Reigns is the only top level heel—assuming that's what he is supposed to be given his current rivalry with Solo Sikoa and LA Knight—on the Red Brand at this point.

Regardless of what role McIntyre plays when he returns, his presence will be welcome since he had been on one of the best runs of his career prior to taking a leave.

Women's Trios Match Potentially Planned for SNME

With just three matches currently official for the upcoming Sunday Night's Main Event show on Sept. 6, WWE could add a women's trios bout to the card.

Per Joey Votes of WrestleVotes (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), WWE has "loosely discussed" putting Fatal Influence vs. Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley on the SNME show.

"I do know the women's trios match—Fatal Influence vs. Alexa, Tatum, and Charlotte—has been loosely discussed to make that card. They are treating this event as a PLE-lite," JoeyVotes said.

The only matches set for the show are Rhodes vs. Orton, Oba Femi vs. Bron Breakker and Baron Corbin vs. Lil Yachty in which Yachty needs to last five minutes to earn Trick Williams a rematch with Corbin for the U.S. title.

WWE has generally put five matches on Saturday Night's Main Event cards, though there have been some exceptions. The Jan. 24 show from Montreal only had three matches take place, though a fourth was scheduled between Rhodes and Fatu that never occurred due to a pre-match brawl.

It would make sense to have the match take place, whether it's on the Sept. 6 card or waiting until Money in the Bank on Oct. 10. Fatal Influence have been feuding with Flair on and off for most of the year. Paxley just recently debuted on SmackDown, so giving her a high-profile match would help elevate her profile.

One thing of note is WWE didn't announce any new matches for SNME during the SmackDown tapings on Monday night for the show airing this week, so the last chance to make it official on the go-home episode on Sept. 4 if it's going to happen.
paragraphs: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Even though it's expected the Saudi Arabia government will present several WWE legends with lucrative financial offers to be involved in WrestleMania 43 in some capacity, The Rock's film schedule might prevent him from being part of the event.
While speaking with Variety 's Jack Dunn and Marc Malkin , Vin Diesel said the current plan is to start filming Fast Forever , the final movie in the Fast & Furious franchise, in December.
"We start shooting in December, if I can make good on the request from the studio," Diesel said.

The Rock, who made a cameo appearance in a mid-credits scene at the end of Fast X , is listed in the cast for the new film despite a previous real-life feud with Diesel that played a part in his absence from the eighth and ninth movies.
Steve Carrier of Ringside News noted the filming schedule, particularly for a production of this size, is likely to last months and could stretch into WrestleMania season.

There are variables that could make it so The Rock has a window in his schedule if he wants to be involved at WrestleMania. No one has said the size of his role in the movie, so it's plausible he won't be needed on set for the entire production.

With Saudi Arabia already believed to be paying $250 million to host WrestleMania next year, the expectation is also that the government will present major financial offers to WWE legends to get them on the card in some capacity.
It was previously reported Saudi officials are preparing an offer to The Rock that would be the largest payday ever given to any wrestler to work a single show in the history of the sport.

WWE has dreamed of a Rock-Roman Reigns match for years. The closest it ever got was in 2024 when the Great One appeared on the first Raw of the year to tease a bout with the Tribal Chief that was then scuttled when Cody Rhodes won the Royal Rumble, though The Rock did wrestle on the show in a tag match.

If The Rock is going to do another match, one would assume he would want it to be sooner than later given that he will turn 55 on May 2 and it requires a lot of physical training to keep his body in the shape to be The Rock everyone thinks of in a WWE ring.
WWE Figuring Out Drew McIntyre's Return Storyline
Having been off WWE television since WrestleMania to work on various outside projects, Drew McIntyre is now waiting for creative to find a story to get him back in the ring.

Per PWInsider Elite (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News), McIntyre is back in the United States after completing work on his other commitments, but WWE's creative team hasn't started plotting out his return at this point.

McIntyre lost to Jacob Fatu in an unsanctioned match at WrestleMania 42. The bout was done to write the Scottish Warrior off television for the time being due to being cast in the Highlander reboot and the Russell Crowe-starring The Last Druid .
The Last Druid started filming in Spain in June. Crowe posted a picture with McIntyre on Instagram on Aug. 5, writing they had recently finished filming.

One thing potentially holding up McIntyre's return is all of the people he was feuding with prior to leaving are embroiled in storylines right now. His last two opponents prior to Fatu were Sami Zayn and Cody Rhodes over the undisputed title.

The decision also has to be made if McIntyre will return as a heel or babyface. If he is staying on SmackDown, it might be better to bring him back as a babyface since they just turned Zayn heel and Randy Orton also returned as a villain.

Of course, the Raw roster also needs an infusion of talent, particularly on the heel side. Roman Reigns is the only top level heel—assuming that's what he is supposed to be given his current rivalry with Solo Sikoa and LA Knight—on the Red Brand at this point.
Regardless of what role McIntyre plays when he returns, his presence will be welcome since he had been on one of the best runs of his career prior to taking a leave.
Women's Trios Match Potentially Planned for SNME
With just three matches currently official for the upcoming Sunday Night's Main Event show on Sept. 6, WWE could add a women's trios bout to the card.
Per Joey Votes of WrestleVotes (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), WWE has "loosely discussed" putting Fatal Influence vs. Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley on the SNME show.
"I do know the women's trios match—Fatal Influence vs. Alexa, Tatum, and Charlotte—has been loosely discussed to make that card. They are treating this event as a PLE-lite," JoeyVotes said.

The only matches set for the show are Rhodes vs. Orton, Oba Femi vs. Bron Breakker and Baron Corbin vs. Lil Yachty in which Yachty needs to last five minutes to earn Trick Williams a rematch with Corbin for the U.S. title.

WWE has generally put five matches on Saturday Night's Main Event cards, though there have been some exceptions. The Jan. 24 show from Montreal only had three matches take place, though a fourth was scheduled between Rhodes and Fatu that never occurred due to a pre-match brawl.

It would make sense to have the match take place, whether it's on the Sept. 6 card or waiting until Money in the Bank on Oct. 10. Fatal Influence have been feuding with Flair on and off for most of the year. Paxley just recently debuted on SmackDown, so giving her a high-profile match would help elevate her profile.

One thing of note is WWE didn't announce any new matches for SNME during the SmackDown tapings on Monday night for the show airing this week, so the last chance to make it official on the go-home episode on Sept. 4 if it's going to happen.

articles.title: Could Connor Hellebuyckâs latest situation leave the Winnipeg Jets facing a difficult NHL decision this summer
articles.summary: NHL News: As training camp approaches, the Winnipeg Jets must navigate Connor Hellebuyck's uncertain future, trade speculation, and the impact on their NHL roster strategy.
articles.body: With the 2026-27 NHL season approaching, the Winnipeg Jets are in a tricky spot with Connor Hellebuyck looming. General manager Kevin Cheveldayoff said in June the organization was taking trade offers for the veteran goaltender, but nothing has come of it.That question became louder after Hellebuyck voiced his disappointment after a disappointing 2025-26 season for Winnipeg. Jets captain Adam Lowry said recently he expects Hellebuyck to report for training camp, suggesting the team is still operating under the assumption its star goaltender is staying in Winnipeg.https://www.instagram.com/p/DcceSwXNsOP/Could Connor Hellebuyckâs future reshape Winnipeg Jets plans this offseason?Connor Hellebuyckâs status might be a big part of the Winnipeg Jetsâ roster strategy, but his return remains the most obvious expectation at this stage. Lowry said Hellebuyck is still a Jet and teammates expect him back for training camp.The situation is a byproduct of Winnipegâs big drop-off last season. The Jets won the Presidentsâ Trophy in 2024-25, but went 35-35-12 and missed the Stanley Cup Playoffs. Hellebuyck also went 23-23-11 with a 2.86 goals-against average and an 895 save percentage.His personal rÃ©sumÃ©, however, remains remarkable. Hellebuyck is a three-time Vezina Trophy winner and helped Team USA win Olympic gold in February 2026.Hellebuyck still has five seasons remaining on a seven-year, $59.5 million deal that averages $8.5 million per year. His no-movement clause also gives him a tonne of leverage on any potential trade.This makes it difficult to trade. Winnipeg would need a deal that would make moving an elite goaltender worth it, and find a way to improve a roster that missed the playoffs.What happens next for the Winnipeg Jets?The immediate answer should be training camp. Lowryâs comments also indicate Winnipeg isnât acting as if a trade is around the corner, while earlier comments from Cheveldayoff suggest the organization is still open to listening.The Jets open their 2026-27 season Oct. 2 at home against the Boston Bruins. If Hellebuyck gets to camp, the trade talk could die down quickly. If thereâs any change to the situation with negotiations or roster developments, his future could again be one of the biggest offseason stories in the league.The latest news suggests Hellebuyck will return to Winnipeg, not a trade on the verge of happening. But the Jetsâ decision is still one to watch until puck drop because moving him would fundamentally change how they approach the season.The future of the Winnipeg Jetsâ Connor Hellebuyck remains one of the biggest stories in the NHL as training camp looms. Winnipeg has fielded trade calls, but captain Adam Lowry expects Hellebuyck to return. Any potential move is complicated by his contract, recent play and elite resume. For now, it looks like the Jets are ready to open the 2026-27 season with their veteran netminder.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bianca Belair Reveals Major Injury Update, WWE Star Has 'No Feeling' in Surgically-Repaired Finger
articles.summary: It's been over a year since WWE Superstar Bianca Belair last wrestled, and it doesn't sound like she'll be back in the ring anytime soon.
articles.body:
It's been over a year since WWE Superstar Bianca Belair last wrestled, and it doesn't sound like she'll be back in the ring anytime soon.

Belair suffered a significant finger injury that required surgery in her last match at WrestleMania 41 in April 2025. After giving birth to her first child during her time off, Belair revealed on Instagram that she's now dealing with carpal tunnel syndrome in both hands.

"No one ever talks about …this stuff … currently carpal tunnel in both hands… fingers completely numb, no feeling in surgery finger whatsoever, no grip strength, and now also Mom thumb… wtf lol," Belair wrote in her Instagram story (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News).

Belair struggled to progress in her recovery from surgery for quite some time, but she dedicated more time to physical therapy during her pregnancy and finally regained the ability to bend her finger. However, she still had visible swelling when she shared an update last month.

Belair was one of WWE's brightest stars and a cornerstone of the women's division, so her presence has been sorely missed. Fans will continue to hope that she will recover and return to reclaim her spot as one of the faces of the company.

articles.title: Matt Cardona Posts Photo from Hospital After Torn Triceps Injury During WWE Main Event Match
articles.summary: Two days after confirming he tore his triceps during a match on Friday night, WWE superstar Matt Cardona was in the hospital.
articles.body:
Two days after confirming he tore his triceps during a match on Friday night, WWE superstar Matt Cardona was in the hospital.

Cardona posted a picture on social media of himself in a hospital bed.

This comes on the heels of Cardona posting an image of his left arm with a wrap on it, announcing he suffered an injury during a match against Kit Wilson taped for Main Event .

The timeline for Cardona to return depends on the severity of the injury. It can take up to one year to get back to full range of motion if surgery is required, though some wrestlers have returned much faster.

Back in 2013, John Cena was out for only two months after undergoing surgery to repair a torn triceps following his SummerSlam match with Daniel Bryan.

Cardona made a few appearances on WWE television while working for TNA last year, but he officially returned to the promotion in January after signing a contract in January.

The former Intercontinental champion has been working on the SmackDown brand with his wife and recently-crowned WWE women's champion Chelsea Green.

articles.title: Beca Telmex 2026: Requisitos, cómo registrarte y monto de los apoyos de Carlos Slim
articles.standfirst: Conoce todos los detalles sobre este apoyo económico
articles.summary: Conoce todos los detalles sobre este apoyo económico
articles.body: Carlos Slim, uno de los empresarios más influyentes de México, sigue sorprendiendo con los apoyos para las personas de nuestro país, ahora con la convocatoria de Becas 2026 de la Fundación Telmex Telcel, un programa que busca impulsar la preparación académica de estudiantes mexicanos. En esta edición, se contempla la entrega de 5 mil becas para quienes cursen una licenciatura, maestría o doctorado en instituciones educativas dentro de la República Mexicana. A través de esta iniciativa, miles de estudiantes mexicanos podrán tener acceso a un apoyo económico que contribuya a su formación profesional, siempre que cumplan con los requisitos establecidos en la convocatoria. El programa contempla a alumnos de licenciatura, maestría y doctorado que destaquen por su desempeño académico y mantengan las condiciones solicitadas durante el tiempo que reciban los depósitos.  Es por ello que en Marca MX te compartimos todos los detalles que debes de saber como registro, requisitos y montos para que puedas aspirar a un ingreso. Para registrarte a la Beca Telmex 2026, primero deberás completar la solicitud correspondiente a través de la página de becas de Fundación Telmex Telcel, utilizando una computadora y siguiendo las indicaciones de la convocatoria. El periodo de registro comenzó el lunes 24 de agosto y permanecerá abierto hasta el martes 22 de septiembre de 2026, por lo que los estudiantes interesados deberán realizar el trámite dentro de estas fechas. Una vez completada la solicitud, el aspirante deberá imprimirla y firmarla, además de reunir todos los documentos solicitados en la convocatoria. Posteriormente, la documentación tendrá que enviarse mediante mensajería especializada al Programa Educativo de Fundación Telmex Telcel, ubicado en Vizcaínas número 16, colonia Centro, alcaldía Cuauhtémoc, Ciudad de México. Es importante considerar que los documentos deberán ser recibidos a más tardar el martes 29 de septiembre de 2026. Para poder solicitar una de las 5 mil Becas Telmex 2026, los estudiantes deberán cumplir con una serie de condiciones académicas y administrativas establecidas en la convocatoria. Entre los principales requisitos se encuentran: Además de cumplir con estos requisitos, los aspirantes deberán proporcionar información y documentación verídica durante el proceso de registro. La Fundación Telmex Telcel señala que cualquier incumplimiento de las condiciones establecidas o la detección de irregularidades en los datos presentados puede ocasionar que la solicitud sea declinada y, en su caso, que el beneficio no continúe. Quienes estén interesados en obtener una de las 5 mil Becas Telmex 2026 deberán prestar atención a dos fechas clave del proceso. El registro en línea estará disponible hasta el martes 22 de septiembre de 2026, mientras que la documentación solicitada tendrá que llegar a Fundación Telmex Telcel a más tardar el 29 de septiembre. Las solicitudes que no cumplan con este último plazo quedarán fuera del proceso de selección. Después de revisar las solicitudes, los resultados de la Beca Telmex 2026 se darán a conocer entre el miércoles 18 y el viernes 27 de noviembre de 2026 a través de la página oficial de Fundación Telmex Telcel. La institución podrá realizar las verificaciones necesarias para confirmar la identidad de los aspirantes y validar los documentos entregados; además, la resolución emitida por el comité encargado de seleccionar a los beneficiarios será definitiva e inapelable.

articles.title: Resultados Melate Retro 1663: números ganadores del martes 25 de agosto 2026
articles.standfirst: Te damos a conocer los números ganadores de este sorteo
articles.summary: Te damos a conocer los números ganadores de este sorteo
articles.body: Es sábado y hoy podría ser un día muy afortunado para todos aquellos que son aficionados del Melate Retro pues para el sorteo 1663 de este 25 de agosto de 2026 tiene una bolsa garantizada de 17.5 millones de pesos. La Lotería Nacional tiene desde hace muchos años los Sorteos Mayor y Especial como los más populares, pero también está Melate que es uno de los más buscados pues además abre las posibilidades de los concursantes para obtener más premios. Como señalamos, Melate cuenta con varias versiones, una de ellas Melate Retro que se juega todos los martes y sábados y este 25 de agosto de 2026 se realizará el sorteo 1663 en punto de las 9 de la noche (Hora del centro de la Ciudad de México). Melate tiene diferentes modalidades, la primera, el Melate tradicional, conocido simplemente como Melate, la segunda es el Melate Revancha, la tercera Melate Revanchita y la última conocida como Melate Retro (se juega los martes y los sábados) y consiste en seleccionar 6 números del 1 al 56. Los ganadores se definen a través de una urna giratoria con 56 esferas. De forma aleatoria son seleccionadas siete esferas, las primeras seis conocidas como los números naturales y la última como el adicional. De tal modo que aquel concursante que en su boleto seleccionó los mismos números será el ganador. articles.title: "Somos swingers": Valeria Marín rompe el silencio de salida de TUDN y la relación Julián Gil & Marc Crosas
articles.standfirst: La conductora señaló que había cumplido una etapa en su carrera
articles.summary: La conductora señaló que había cumplido una etapa en su carrera
articles.body: Un par de semanas después de anunciar de manera sorpresiva su salida de TUDN, la conductora Valeria Marín finalmente reveló los motivos por los que decidió no continuar en Televisa después de la cobertura de la Copa del Mundo y también aclaró los rumores de su salida y una supuesta relación con el analista de esa misma cadena deportiva, Marc Crosas. Recordemos que hace un par de semanas, tras el anuncio de su salida de TUDN, comenzaron a circular varias versiones sobre las razones por las que no continuará en Televisa, entre ellas, se habló de una petición de aumento de sueldo, que habría provocado que tomará la decisión de no continuar luego de 7 años en esa empresa. Valeria Marín llegó a TUDN hace 7 años y señaló que después de pensarlo y cerrar la cobertura de la Copa del Mundo tomó la decisión de salir de la cadena deportiva y además aseguró estar contenta de haber dado un paso al costado. "Después del Mundial, después de pensarlo, dije 'me despido con una cobertura increíble', yo creo que ya hice lo que tenía que hacer en este lugar, el lugar también me dio lo que me tenía que haber dado o lo que me gané y sería bonito cerrarlo en lo más alto. Estoy súper feliz con la decisión que tomé y muy emocionada por lo que se pueda venir". Estas declaraciones las hizo en el podcast 'Sabor a Fútbol', en donde también hizo referencia un par de veces a su pareja, el actor Julián Gil quien según las palabras de la conductora le dio un par de consejos antes de tomar la decisión de salir de TUDN: "Me dijo ' no pongas todos los huevos en la misma canasta', y sí, estoy dejando a la televisora más fuerte en México pero ver que hay un mundo mucho más grande, en donde puedes tener muchas más opciones Desde luego uno de los puntos más atractivos del poscast fue cuando hablaron sobre los rumores que rodearon su salida de TUDN, incluido un aparente romance con el panelista Marc Crosas y también el aumento de sueldo que derivó en la decisión que tomó: "Yo di todo, ellos me dieron todo. Yo quiero más como cualquier profesional, siempre aspiramos a más, quizás el canal no me lo puede dar". Y cuando se le preguntó sobre la relación que algunos rumores instalaron con su compañero en TUDN, respondió a manera de broma: "Confieso que somos pareja swinger, Marc si entra en la ecuación pero salgo de la cancha yo y entre Marc, entonces son 'Juli' y Marc", al tiempo en el que comenzó a reírse, "esas veriones ni las aclaro y dan risa, la gente no está preparada para esta conversación".
